title: Childhood trauma, resilience and suicide risk among patients with schizophrenia: Cross-sectional direct and indirect associations with current depressive and anxiety symptoms.
abstract: This study examined associations between childhood trauma, current depressive and anxiety symptoms, resilience, and suicidal risk among Vietnamese patients with schizophrenia, including cross-sectional indirect associations. A total of 581 clinically stable patients with schizophrenia (62.0% male; mean age = 40.35 ± 11.23 years) were recruited from multiple psychiatric facilities in Vietnam. Participants completed the Childhood Trauma Questionnaire-Short Form (CTQ-SF), Patient Health Questionnaire-4 (PHQ-4), Brief Resilience Scale (BRS), and Suicidal Behaviors Questionnaire-Revised (SBQ-R). Consistent partial least squares structural equation modeling (PLSc-SEM) with 5000 BCa bootstrap samples was used to estimate direct, indirect, and exploratory interaction associations. Generalized additive models and restricted cubic splines were used to explore nonlinear associations. Childhood trauma was positively associated with current depressive and anxiety symptoms (β = .256, p < .001) and suicidal risk (β = .194, p = .003). Current depressive and anxiety symptoms were associated with suicidal risk (β = .242, p = .001), and the indirect association from childhood trauma through current depressive and anxiety symptoms was significant (β = .062, p = .009). Resilience was associated with fewer current depressive and anxiety symptoms (β = -.323, p < .001) and showed a significant indirect association with lower suicidal risk through current depressive and anxiety symptoms (β = -.078, p = .004), but its direct association and both interaction terms were not significant. The full-sample PHQ-4 nonlinear finding was not robust in upper-tail sensitivity analyses, and no CTQ-SF threshold was supported. Childhood trauma showed both a direct association with suicidal risk and an indirect association through current depressive and anxiety symptoms. Resilience was indirectly associated with lower suicidal risk through fewer PHQ-4 symptoms, but neither its direct association with suicide risk nor its moderating role was statistically significant. These cross-sectional findings do not establish temporal or causal pathways.

title: Structural food access inequalities and aging transitions: A geospatial, multistate and longitudinal analysis of UK Biobank.
abstract: The food environment may influence neurodegeneration and mortality. This study examined associations of food deserts (FD) with brain health and survival using UK Biobank data. We analyzed 262,847 participants aged ≥50 years at baseline (2006-2010) with linked geospatial (2018-2020), neuroimaging (2014-2023; 2019-2023), dietary, biological, and health data. FD exposure was aggregated at the local authority (LA) level. Outcomes included incident dementia, Parkinson's disease (PD), and all-cause mortality (ACM) from January 1, 2020, to January 1, 2024. Neuroimaging sub-analyses (n = 2429) assessed brain volumes and white matter microstructure (WMM) using diffusion MRI metrics (FAmean, MDmean, ICVFmean, ISOVFmean, ODmean). Cox, multistate survival, and mixed-effects models were used. Spatial clustering examined co-localization between FD and outcomes. Area-level FD was examined as the primary exposure, with FI evaluated mainly as a secondary effect modifier. Women had lower FD and FI scores and better cardiovascular and social health. FD (per SD increase) was associated with higher ACM risk (HR = 1.06; 95% CI: 1.02-1.09) after adjustment for demographics and deprivation, attenuating after full adjustment. FD also predicted faster WMM decline among women (ODmean β = +0.1124; p = 0.028), though neuroimaging associations did not survive FDR correction. Spatial analyses revealed threefold higher odds of concordance between FD and ACM, and between FD and FAmean decline. FI did not modify FD-ACM associations. Living in food deserts was linked to higher mortality and faster white matter decline, particularly among women. Findings highlight the role of area-level food environments in brain health and aging.

title: Mobilization patterns and physical activity in hospitalized individuals with moderate to severe acquired brain injury: a prospective observational study.
journal: Annals of physical and rehabilitation medicine
abstract: Upright time is an important component in early rehabilitation following moderate to severe acquired brain injury (ABI); however, objective in-hospital data are scarce. This study quantified upright time during inpatient rehabilitation using triaxial accelerometry. To characterize mobilization and physical activity during early and late rehabilitation phases in individuals with moderate to severe ABI. Prospective cohort study in a tertiary neurorehabilitation facility. Adults (≥18 years) with moderate to severe ABI (Glasgow Coma Scale score 1 h), admitted between Nov 2022 and Jan 2024. Accelerometer data were collected for 7 days (7 AM to 10 PM) at 2 time points: early (T1) and late admission (T2). The primary outcome was upright time. Other outcomes included associations between clinical characteristics and upright time, and between early upright time and functional outcomes at discharge. Ninety-nine participants were enrolled; 58 provided sufficient activity data at both time points. Median upright time was 8 min/day (IQR, 3; 30) at T1, increasing to 43 min/day (IQR 22; 131) at T2 (+6.6 percentage points, 95% CI 4.3 to 8.9). Shorter upright time at T1 was associated with the confusional state and medical device attachment, and at T2, with spasmolytic and sedative treatments. Longer upright time at T1 was associated with improved Functional Ambulation Category (β = 0.17 per % increase, 95% CI 0.08 to 0.27), and Functional Independence Measure, motor subscale (β = 3.01, 95% CI 0.77 to 5.25). Missing activity data were substantial (41% excluded). Upright time increased during rehabilitation but remained low overall. Medical devices were associated with reduced upright time, and more early upright time showed potential links to higher walking ability and greater independence in mobility at discharge. These findings underscore the need for tailored interventions, real-time feedback, and clinical guidelines to optimize mobilization during rehabilitation. NCT05571462.

title: From affect to rules: A conceptual model of compensation in prodromal behavioral frontotemporal degeneration.
journal: Cortex; a journal devoted to the study of the nervous system and behavior
abstract: Behavioral-variant frontotemporal dementia (bvFTD) is typically described in terms of progressive loss of social and behavioral control. However, the earliest stages of the disease may also involve active, developed forms of compensation that remain largely invisible to standard assessment. These strategies are rarely characterized, yet they may offer a unique entry point into the mechanisms by which social functioning is temporarily preserved despite emerging degeneration. Here, I report a longitudinal single-case study of a young C9orf72 repeat-expansion carrier followed from the prodromal stage to established moderate bvFTD. Based on more than a dozen hours of semi-structured interviews initiated at symptom emergence, thematic analysis identified five compensatory subthemes. Together, these strategies suggested a coherent shift in the architecture of behavioral control that remain largely invisible to standard medical or neuropsychological assessment. As implicit, flexible, and internally sustained regulation became less reliable, functioning appeared to rely on control processes that were more explicit, environmentally distributed, routine-based, and effortful. These observations can be organized around three broader principles: explicitation, externalization, and stabilization. The case suggests that early preservation in bvFTD may reflect not only residual capacities, but also an active and fragile reorganization of social and behavioral control. By foregrounding the patient's own compensatory work, this study provides a hypothesis-generating conceptual framework for understanding how everyday functioning may be maintained during the prodromal-to-dementia transition, and highlights qualitative longitudinal single-case designs and participatory research as a powerful tool for identifying hidden forms of adaptation in neurodegenerative disease and refine theoretical models of social behavior.

title: Torijaponanes A-N, structurally diverse sesquiterpenoids from Torilis japonica with anti-inflammatory activity via suppression of NF-κB and MAPK activation.
abstract: Fourteen previously undescribed sesquiterpenoids with diverse skeletons, including one carabrane-type (1), one eudesmane-type (2) and twelve germacrane-type derivatives (3-7, 10-14, 16, 17), along with eleven known sesquiterpenoids (8, 9, 15, 18-25), were isolated from the fruit of Torilis japonica. Their planar structures were established by NMR, HR-ESI-MS, IR and UV spectroscopy, while the absolute configurations were determined by ECD calculations and single-crystal X-ray diffraction. Notably, compound 1 is the first carabrane-type sesquiterpenoid reported from the genus Torilis, compound 2 is a previously undescribed eudesmane-type sesquiterpenoid bearing hemiterpenoic acid substituents at C-6 and C-8, and 10-12 possess a germacrane skeleton featuring an oxygen-bridged ring between C-11 and C-13. In bioactivity assays, compounds 6, 7, 8, 10, 12, 14, 15 and 21 markedly suppressed LPS-stimulated NO production in RAW 264.7 macrophages, with IC50 values of 6.92-16.00 μM, comparable to or better than dexamethasone (IC50 = 16.74 μM). Compound 7, the most potent derivative (IC50 = 6.92 μM), markedly downregulated the mRNA levels of key pro-inflammatory mediators, including IL-6, TNF-α, iNOS, and IL-1β. Mechanistically, compound 7 inhibited the NF-κB/MAPK pathway, and modulated the expression of selected M1/M2 macrophage markers under distinct stimulation conditions. Collectively, this study expands the structural diversity of sesquiterpenoids from T. japonica and highlights compound 7 as a promising anti-inflammatory agent.

title: Association between nasogastric tube placement and self-reported anxiety/depression symptoms in patients receiving endovascular thrombectomy for large vessel occlusion: A post-hoc analysis of the ENCHANTED2/MT trial.
journal: Journal of clinical neuroscience : official journal of the Neurosurgical Society of Australasia
abstract: Post-stroke anxiety and depression are common after endovascular thrombectomy (EVT) for large vessel occlusion (LVO) and impair long-term recovery. Nasogastric tube (NGT) placement marks severe dysphagia and illness, but its association with anxiety or depression remains unclear. We aimed to evaluate whether NGT placement is associated with the presence and severity of 90-day self-reported anxiety/depression symptoms after successful EVT. We performed a post-hoc analysis of the ENCHANTED2/MT multicentre randomized controlled trial, including patients with anterior-circulation LVO who achieved successful reperfusion and had complete 90-day EQ-5D-3 L data. Participants were stratified by in-hospital NGT placement (No-NGT group vs. NGT group). The primary outcome was self-reported anxiety/depression assessed by the EQ-5D-3 L dimension (no, moderate, or extreme symptoms). We explored the association between NGT placement and the proportion and severity of self-reported anxiety/depression using propensity score matching (PSM) and logistic regression, and performed exploratory subgroup analyses. Of 575 patients, 280(48.7%) received an NGT. Before matching, the proportion reporting self-reported anxiety/depression symptoms was 38.6% in the NGT group versus 15.6% in the no-NGT group (unadjusted OR3.40, 95%CI 2.30-5.09). After adjustment for measured clinical covariates, the association remained significant (adjusted OR2.97, 95%CI 1.93-4.63; ordinal OR3.06, 95%CI 1.99-4.77). After PSM, 175 patients were matched in each group; NGT placement remained associated with higher odds of self-reported anxiety/depression symptoms (37.7% vs 21.1%; OR2.26, 95%CI 1.41-3.65; ordinal OR2.25, 95%CI 1.41-3.63). In exploratory subgroup analyses, the association appeared more pronounced in patients with admission NIHSS ≤ 15 (OR3.83, 95% CI1.82-8.07; P for interaction = 0.049). In this post-hoc analysis, NGT placement was associated with higher odds of self-reported anxiety/depression symptoms.NGT requirement may identify patients who deserve closer psychological assessment.

title: Postural adjustments in standing and gait reflect amnestic mild cognitive impairment.
abstract: Amnestic mild cognitive impairment (aMCI), a prodromal stage of Alzheimer's disease, may involve subtle motor alterations preceding overt cognitive decline. Because postural alignment integrates multisensory and executive control systems, it may reveal early motor-cognitive disruption. This study aimed to identify posture-related features associated with cognition and to determine whether individuals with aMCI exhibit distinct standing and gait kinematics. In this cross-sectional observational study, 14 older adults with aMCI and 14 age-matched cognitively healthy controls underwent three-dimensional motion analysis during quiet standing and level walking. Segmental angles and temporospatial gait parameters were analysed. Cognitive performance was assessed using standardised neuropsychological tests. Group comparisons and exploratory partial correlation analyses adjusted for age and education were performed. The aMCI group exhibited reduced lumbar extension (p = 0.020), pelvic anterior tilt (p = 0.012), and hip flexion (p = 0.016) during standing. While lumbopelvic deviations persisted during gait (p ≤ 0.011), hip flexion and temporospatial parameters were comparable between groups. In controls, verbal episodic memory correlated positively with lumbopelvic alignment (r = 0.67-0.80, p ≤ 0.02). In aMCI, greater hip flexion during gait was associated with poor verbal fluency (r = -0.57, p = 0.05) and visual memory (r = -0.68, p = 0.02). Lumbopelvic alignment was closely linked to episodic memory in cognitively normal ageing, but this coupling appeared disrupted in aMCI, with motor-cognitive associations shifting toward hip-mediated compensatory or reorganised gait control. These kinematic markers were detectable despite preserved gait speed and may be more sensitive than conventional temporospatial gait measures under steady-state conditions. Longitudinal studies are warranted.

title: PFAS-induced blood-brain barrier dysfunction: A neurovascular perspective.
abstract: Per- and polyfluoroalkyl substances (PFAS) are persistent environmental contaminants widely detected in human circulation, yet their neurotoxic mechanisms remain incompletely understood. Emerging evidence suggests that the blood-brain barrier (BBB) may represent an important site of PFAS interaction alongside the brain parenchyma. Cerebral endothelial cells are continuously exposed to circulating PFAS, which has been associated with oxidative stress, inflammatory activation, alterations in tight junction organization, and increased barrier permeability. Although these effects may occur without extensive endothelial cell death or gross structural damage to the vascular architecture, most currently available PFAS studies report measurable molecular or functional alterations of the BBB. Direct evidence for neurovascular signaling in the complete absence of detectable barrier dysfunction remains limited. Here, we propose a neurovascular framework in which PFAS-induced endothelial dysfunction may trigger signaling cascades that propagate across the neurovascular unit (NVU), affecting pericytes, astrocytes, and microglia. This propagation can be understood as a coordinated, multiscale process influenced by endothelial signaling rather than direct neuronal exposure alone, potentially contributing to a self-reinforcing cycle of neurovascular dysfunction. This perspective highlights an interface-driven mechanism centered on the BBB, complementing existing parenchyma-focused models. Despite increasing support for this framework, critical gaps remain. Most mechanistic evidence is derived from a limited subset of legacy PFAS, particularly PFOS and PFOA, raising concerns regarding generalizability to emerging compounds. In addition, existing experimental models often fail to capture the multicellular complexity and chronic exposure conditions relevant to human physiology. Addressing these limitations will require the development of human-relevant neurovascular models capable of resolving endothelial responses and their downstream effects. Collectively, this framework provides a conceptual basis for linking chronic low-dose PFAS exposure to neurovascular dysfunction and supports the development of more human-relevant risk assessment strategies.

title: Greater eccentric hamstrings to concentric quadriceps strength ratio at 6 months after anterior cruciate ligament reconstruction is associated with reduced odds of revision within 2 years.
journal: Knee surgery, sports traumatology, arthroscopy : official journal of the ESSKA
abstract: To investigate the association between eccentric hamstrings-to-concentric quadriceps strength ratio (mixed hamstrings to quadriceps [HQ]-strength ratio) at 6 months postoperatively and revision anterior cruciate ligament reconstruction (ACL-R) within 2 years of primary surgery. The secondary purpose was to investigate the association between the mixed HQ-strength ratio and single-leg hop for distance limb symmetry index (LSI). Data were collected from a local registry at Capio Artro Clinic, Stockholm, Sweden. Patients aged ≥15 years, without concomitant ligament injuries and meniscal resection or repair who underwent primary ACL-R with hamstring tendon autografts between 2005 and 2021 were included. Isokinetic eccentric hamstrings and concentric quadriceps strength were assessed using a Biodex dynamometer 6 months postoperatively. Associations between mixed HQ-strength ratio on the ACL-R leg and revision ACL-R were analysed using multivariable logistic regression analysis, presented with odds ratios (ORs), 95% confidence intervals (CIs) and area under the receiver operating characteristics curve (AUC). Associations between mixed HQ-strength ratio and single-leg hop for distance LSI were analysed with linear regression. Of the 3458 patients included, 49.5% were female and the mean age was 28.8 ± 10.4 years. Patients who underwent revision ACL-R within 2 years had lower mixed HQ-strength ratio on the ACL-R leg 6 months postoperatively. After adjustment for age at primary ACL-R and preinjury Tegner level, each 10-unit increase in the mixed HQ-strength ratio on the ACL-R leg was associated with lower odds of revision ACL-R (OR = 0.81, 95% CI [0.71;0.93], p = 0.003). However, the discriminatory ability was poor (AUC = 0.64). A greater mixed HQ-strength ratio was associated with poorer single-leg hop for distance LSI, adjusted for age at primary ACL-R and preinjury Tegner level (β = -1.30, 95% CI [-1.51;-1.09], p < 0.001). The mixed HQ-strength ratio may complement the evaluation of muscle strength recovery after ACL-R. However, its poor discriminatory ability limits its use to identify patients who will undergo revision ACL-R. Level III.

title: Optimizing myelin water imaging in multiple sclerosis.
abstract: Myelin water imaging (MWI) allows in vivo quantification of myelin content using MRI. Multi-echo gradient-echo (MEGRE) sequences with Variable Flip Angles (VFA), combined with diffusion-weighted imaging (DWI), can generate robust, whole-brain myelin water fraction (MWF) maps more efficiently than conventional implementations. We evaluated how spatial resolution and number of flip angles affect MWI quality in a clinical research setting. Fifteen people with MS and ten healthy controls were scanned at 3 T (Siemens VIDA). MRI included multi-shell DWI and 3D-MEGRE acquired at 2.0 mm and 2.5 mm isotropic resolution. Twelve echoes were acquired at five flip angles. MWF was quantified based on a three-compartment T1, T2*, and DWI model, and determined in normal appearing white matter (NAWM), lesions and corpus callosum. Associations between MWF across resolutions and VFA schemes were assessed using Bland-Altman, ICC-C and ICC-AA. MWF was highest in corpus callosum (10.2 ± 1.1%), intermediate in NAWM (7.9 ± 0.7%), and lowest in lesions (4.9 ± 0.7%) (values for 2.0 mm and FA5). A FA4 MEGRE protocol showed comparable MWF values, while FA3 systematically overestimated MWF and showed greater variability, particularly in lesions. ICC-C between spatial resolutions was good to excellent (0.80-0.91), ICC-AA was moderate to good (0.66-0.81), indicating that the two resolutions should not be treated interchangeably. QC monitoring of fitting results is recommended to strengthen reliability of MWF results. MWI duration can be shortened with a FA4 MEGRE protocol. Resolution choice should be guided by study aims, as 2.0 mm and 2.5 mm were not fully interchangeable.

title: Diagnostic accuracy of Neuromelanin-sensitive MRI for Parkinson Disease: A systematic review and meta-analysis.
abstract: Objective: The diagnosis of Parkinson's disease (PD) remains challenging due to clinical overlap with other parkinsonian syndromes and the absence of widely available imaging biomarkers. Neuromelanin-sensitive MRI (NM-MRI) enables in vivo visualization of neuromelanin in the substantia nigra (SN) and locus coeruleus (LC), where signal loss reflects dopaminergic neurodegeneration in the SN and noradrenergic neurodegeneration in the LC. This systematic review and meta-analysis aimed to evaluate the diagnostic accuracy of NM-MRI in differentiating PD from healthy controls. PubMed, Embase, and the Cochrane Library were searched from inception to February 2025. Studies evaluating the diagnostic accuracy of NM-MRI in PD versus healthy controls were included. Two independent reviewers extracted data and assessed methodological quality using QUADAS-2. Pooled sensitivity and specificity were estimated using a random-effects bivariate model, with construction of a summary receiver operating characteristic (SROC) curve. Subgroup analyses were performed by anatomical region (SN, LC) and imaging parameter (volume, area, signal intensity, contrast ratio, subjective assessment), along with meta-regression and Deeks' funnel plot for publication bias. This review was registered in PROSPERO (CRD420251088071). Twenty-eight studies comprising 2,268 participants were included. Pooled sensitivity and specificity were 88.0 % (95 % CI, 85.3-90.2 %) and 84.4 % (95 % CI, 80.6-87.5 %), respectively, with an area under the SROC curve of 0.901 and low heterogeneity (I2 = 3.6 % for sensitivity, 9.2 % for specificity). Volumetric analysis of the SN yielded robust and reproducible performance (sensitivity 88.0 %, specificity 85.5 %), while subjective visual assessment achieved the highest sensitivity (90.8 %) but lower reproducibility. Meta-regression identified no significant effect of MRI acquisition parameters on diagnostic accuracy, and no significant publication bias was detected. NM-MRI demonstrates high diagnostic accuracy for differentiating PD from healthy controls, with volumetric analysis of the substantia nigra offering a robust and reproducible imaging biomarker. As the included studies compared PD with healthy controls rather than with other parkinsonian syndromes, these findings should not yet be extrapolated to the differential diagnosis of PD from other forms of parkinsonism.

title: ISR addiction: Co-opting a stress sentinel to fuel tumor resilience and therapy resistance.
abstract: The integrated stress response (ISR), a conserved cellular sentinel, is pathologically commandeered in cancer to sustain survival under chronic duress. Here, we posit that tumors evolve a state of "ISR Addiction", a profound, non-oncogenic dependency on persistent ISR signaling orchestrated through sustained eIF2α phosphorylation and ATF4-driven transcription. We delineate a three-stage continuum-utilization, dependence, and fixation-tracing how this addiction emerges under microenvironmental pressure and becomes entrenched during therapy. This dependency actively fuels metastasis and acts as a central hub for resistance to chemotherapy, targeted agents, and immunotherapy. Expanding this view, we embed ISR addiction within a multilayered "Ecosystem of Tumor Addictions", where bidirectional crosstalk with redox addiction (maintaining biochemical balance) and neural addiction (processing systemic signals) collectively creates a buffered resilience network. Crucially, this ecosystem reveals a therapeutically exploitable fragility: the addicted state is maintained in a precarious "Goldilocks" balance ("Goldilocks" refers to a "just right" condition-not too much, not too little-borrowed from the children's tale Goldilocks and the Three Bears, where the protagonist finds the porridge that is neither too hot nor too cold, but perfectly suited), susceptible to either "enforced withdrawal" (blocking pro-survival ATF4 outputs) or "toxic overload" (hyperactivating the pro-apoptotic CHOP arm). We propose that rational combinations targeting this addiction network, particularly with standard-of-care or immunomodulatory agents, offer a transformative strategy to dismantle the resilient core of advanced malignancies.

title: MRgFUS for drug-resistant epilepsy: Preliminary report for prospective clinical trial.
abstract: To assess the safety, feasibility, and preliminary clinical outcomes of magnetic resonance-guided focused ultrasound (MRgFUS) for drug-resistant epilepsy (DRE). This TFDA-regulated, open-label study enrolled four adults with DRE. MRgFUS targeted the anterior nucleus of the thalamus (ANT), the centromedian nucleus (CM), the posterior corpus callosum (CC), or the hypothalamic hamartoma (HH). The primary endpoints were safety and feasibility, while secondary endpoints included seizure frequency, EEG results, and postoperative MRI findings. The mean age of the patients was 34.7 years and the mean SDR was 0.38. Two of the procedures were performed under local anesthesia and three under general anesthesia. No serious adverse events, permanent neurological deficit, or postoperative cognitive decline were observed. At follow-up ranging from 3 to 15 months, seizure outcomes varied. The CM-treated patient showed stable overall seizure frequency with a 42.6% reduction in focal seizures. Posterior CC lesioning reduced interhemispheric EEG synchrony and was associated with a 15.9% reduction in generalized seizures. The HH case displayed a decrease in epileptiform activity on EEG and a 55.5% reduction of gelastic seizures, despite the absence of a definitive lesion. In the ANT case, the initial procedure was discontinued prior to reaching therapeutic temperatures, and the repeat treatment under general anesthesia was associated with a 66.0% seizure reduction at final follow-up. MRgFUS achieved lesion formation at selected epilepsy-related targets, including the first reported applications to the posterior CC and CM for epilepsy. However, the ability to achieve therapeutic temperatures and produce a definitive lesion varied among patients and was influenced by skull characteristics of the anatomical target. Given the small, heterogeneous cohort and limited follow-up, the observed clinical outcomes should be considered preliminary. Larger studies with longer follow-up are needed to establish efficacy and optimize treatment parameters.

title: Imaging fast neural circuit activity in brain and nerve with Electrical Impedance Tomography (fnEIT): review, method and engineering aspects.
abstract: Fast neural electrical impedance tomography (fnEIT) is a technique for imaging neural activity in brains or nerves, with a resolution of milliseconds and millimetres, using an applied current and boundary or depth voltage measurement. Proof of principle has been demonstrated in animal studies, but it is yet to be adopted into common use. Objective The purpose of this review is to provide an introduction and overview of the method and technical aspects of fnEIT research and its place in the biomedical sciences. Topics covered include bioimpedance of action potentials, fnEIT studies to date, similar EIT methods and technical innovations. Approach A critical review of the fnEIT literature has been performed. Promising areas of future work and their applications are highlighted, including challenges that must be overcome. Main Results It is shown that the fields of nerve imaging and neuromodulation, cognitive neuroscience in animals and humans, and epileptic seizure localisation could benefit from the ability of fnEIT to image millisecond scale neuronal depolarization throughout brain or nerve. This is achievable with existing methods but with current limitations of the need for implanted cranial or nerve electrodes and averaging to a repeated stimulus. Current approaches to overcome this include CMOS integrated active electrodes, frequency division multiplexing for parallel signal acquisition, and recording with atomic magnetometers. With these, it is a realistic possibility to achieve non-invasive imaging of fast neural activity in real-time with an electrode-atomic magnetometer helmet in human subjects with a resolution of mm and msec. Significance. This review serves as a general guide for those working in related fields or those considering the use of EIT. With the above advances, it is a realistic possibility to achieve non-invasive imaging of fast neural activity in real-time with an electrode-atomic magnetometer helmet in human subjects with a resolution of mm and msec.

title: Disentangling homogeneous and heterogeneous representation of human functional connectome via graph learning.
abstract: Functional connectivity analysis of fMRI data provides critical insight into large-scale brain organization; however, conventional approaches often ignore the specific information mixed with population-level structure and individual- or condition-specific variability. We aimed to develop an interpretable framework that separates these shared and heterogeneous components of the human functional connectome.Approach.We developed Joint Individual Graph Learning (JIGL), a multi-view graph learning framework that jointly estimates a low-rank common graph and sparse view-specific graphs across subjects or experimental conditions. We evaluated JIGL using resting-state and task-based fMRI data from 422 individuals across eight conditions and compared it with Pearson correlation, SIMLR (CIMLR), and Simplex. Performance was assessed using alignment with established resting-state network organization, associations with age and cognitive phenotypes, task identifiability, and low-dimensional representations of task-specific connectivity.Main results.The common graph learned by JIGL captured a biologically meaningful functional backbone and showed stronger alignment with established resting-state network organization than the comparison methods. JIGL-derived individual graphs preserved biologically relevant inter-individual variability, yielding stronger associations with age and cognitive phenotypes. The task-specific graphs also showed improved identifiability, as quantified by the intraclass correlation coefficient. Furthermore, low-dimensional embeddings of the connectivity matrices revealed structured, network-dependent task signatures that were consistently distinct from both the common graph and the resting-state condition.Significance.JIGL provides a principled framework for disentangling shared functional architecture from individual- and condition-specific connectivity patterns. This decomposition improves sensitivity to biologically meaningful variability and supports more interpretable analyses of functional brain organization across individuals and cognitive states.&#xD.

title: Assessing the Effectiveness, Engagement, and Acceptability of a Smartwatch Healthy Lifestyle Intervention for Cognitive Enhancement in Healthy Adults: Mixed Methods Electroencephalography Protocol.
abstract: Wearable technologies are rapidly transforming the health care landscape by enabling the tracking of real-time physiological and behavioral data used in healthy lifestyle interventions. Despite their widespread adoption in the consumer market, scientific validation of their impact on the brain remains limited, and factors influencing effects on cognition and adherence are not fully understood. This gap is critical, as consumers, health care providers, and researchers depend on these data to unlock the potential of wearables for cognitive support. We aim to assess the effectiveness, engagement, and acceptability of a commercially available smartwatch healthy lifestyle intervention on cognitive enhancement in healthy adults, using a convergent parallel mixed methods design. We seek to provide a comprehensive, replicable methodological framework to evaluate wearable technology interventions targeting cognitive enhancement in healthy adults. Healthy adults aged 18 to 40 years with a sedentary lifestyle (N=72) interested in participating in a healthy lifestyle intervention will be recruited in the Vancouver Metropolitan Area, BC, Canada. Participants will be randomly assigned into an intervention group using an Apple Watch or a control group following standard physical activity guidelines without an Apple Watch for a period of 4 weeks. Effectiveness will be evaluated through (1) cognitive function (primary outcome)-executive function, specifically inhibitory control, via electroencephalogram-based event-related potentials (N2/P3) during a go/no-go task; (2) resting-state brain activity via electroencephalogram spectral power; (3) behavioral performance (reaction time and accuracy); (4) perceived health (36-item Short Form Health Survey); and (5) qualitative analysis of factors affecting the intervention's effectiveness. Engagement will be assessed through goal completion metrics and qualitative analysis of barriers, facilitators, and usage patterns. Acceptability will be assessed through System Usability Scale scores and qualitative analysis of factors affecting usability, satisfaction, and user preferences. This design integrates assessments before, during, and after intervention. Qualitative assessments will include weekly check-ins and semistructured interviews to obtain a comprehensive understanding of factors influencing the effectiveness, engagement, and acceptability of the intervention. Exploratory outcomes include descriptions of possible interactions between the 3 constructs and comparison of smartwatch-tracked vs self-reported goal completion. The study received funding from the AGE-WELL Network Centres of Excellence (April 2020-March 2023) and was approved by the Simon Fraser University Research Ethics Board. Enrollment for the study is ongoing. As of October 2026, data have been collected from 48 participants and are currently being processed and analyzed. The first results are expected to be published in 2027. This study outlines a foundational framework for evaluating the effectiveness, engagement, and acceptability of wearable health interventions targeting cognitive enhancement in healthy adults. Furthermore, our mixed methods approach with randomized controlled comparison is expected to inform the design and development of effective, engaging, and friendly wearable brain health technologies.

title: The (amide-)N-methylnicotinamide is a microbe-derived NAD+ precursor that drives gut stem cell renewal.
abstract: Nicotinamide Adenine Dinucleotide (NAD) is a critical cellular coenzyme whose decline associates with various chronic and inflammatory diseases. Improved NAD restoration may reduce disease risks and extend healthy lifespan. We report here that certain commensal bacteria including specific probiotic species produce (amide-)N-methylnicotinamide (N-MNA), which is a structural isomer of methylnicotinamide, a nicotinamide degradative metabolite. Patients with gut dysbiosis and inflammation show reduced stool N-MNA. Stable isotope tracing revealed that N-MNA can be rapidly taken up and incorporated into NAD redox reactions by intestinal epithelial cells (IECs) and non-IECs of fruit fly, mouse, and human. Genetic and pharmacological analyses suggest that N-MNA is converted to NAD+ via the Preiss-Handler pathway, independent of the salvage pathway. Cell-type-specific ablation or overexpression of SIRT1, an NAD-consuming enzyme, in Drosophila, along with intestinal stem cell (ISC) lineage tracing in mice revealed that systemic N-MNA supplementation promotes ISC regeneration and gut epithelial repair. Compared to known NAD precursors, N-MNA brings a methyl group into host cells, representing a class of microbe-derived NAD precursor that stimulates the tissue regenerative power.

title: CD8+ T cells induce RIPK1-regulated brain endothelial cell death in cerebral malaria.
abstract: Cerebral malaria (CM) is a potentially lethal complication of Plasmodium falciparum infection characterized by blood-brain barrier disruption and brain hemorrhage. Although immune-mediated endothelial damage is central to CM pathology, the mechanisms linking cytotoxic immune responses to endothelial injury remain unclear. Here, we show that CD8+ T cells induce receptor-interacting serine/threonine-protein kinase 1 (RIPK1)-regulated cell death of brain endothelial cells in mouse CM, while RIPK1 phosphorylation is increased in brain endothelial cells in human CM. Using magnetic resonance imaging, three-dimensional tissue-cleared brain imaging, cross-species pathology, endothelial translatomics, immunocerebrovascular interactomics, and genetic association testing, we identify a CD8+ T cell-dependent, RIPK1-centered mouse endothelial cell death program. Combined RIPK1 and caspase inhibition protected cross-presenting endothelial cells from CD8+ T cell-mediated death in vitro. In vivo, brain endothelial-specific genetic inactivation or systemic pharmacological inhibition of RIPK1 kinase activity prolonged survival in mouse CM without altering parasitemia. These findings support RIPK1 inhibition as a promising therapeutic strategy to counter CD8+ T cell-induced endothelial death in CM.

title: Brainstem enkephalinergic neural circuit underlying cold-induced pain relief in mice.
abstract: Application of cold or cold-mimicking chemicals to injury has long been recognized as an effective means of pain relief. However, underlying neural mechanisms remain elusive. Here, we identified a cold-responsive neuronal subset within the lateral parabrachial nucleus (lPBN), the thermosensory relay region in the hindbrain, that mediates cold-induced analgesia in mice. Activation of these neurons and their projection to ventrolateral periaqueductal gray (vlPAG) increased the nociceptive threshold, while ablation of these neurons attenuated analgesia induced by cold-mimicking chemicals. We further identified that these neurons express precursor gene of enkephalin (Penk), which is necessary for TRPM8 (transient receptor potential melastatin 8)-mediated pain relief. Mechanistically, cold-responsive lPBN neurons frequency-dependently released enkephalin peptide into vlPAG to activate the descending pain modulation circuitry via disinhibition. Activation of cold-responsive neurons reduced spinal cord responses to noxious stimuli, suggesting the involvement of a top-down pain modulation pathway. These findings propose a central mechanism underlying cold-induced pain relief, which could be a novel therapeutic target.

title: Intravenous midazolam alters short-interval paired-pulse TMS responses differently in younger and older adults.
abstract: Aging is associated with changes in cortical excitability and altered responsiveness to benzodiazepines, but the effects of benzodiazepine challenge on motor cortical paired-pulse physiology in older adults remain incompletely understood. We examined whether intravenous midazolam differentially modulates corticospinal excitability and short-interval paired-pulse transcranial magnetic stimulation (TMS) responses in younger and older adults. Sixteen younger adults (18-35 years) and sixteen older adults (50-69 years) underwent single-pulse and paired-pulse (conditioning stimulus: 110% motor threshold; test stimulus: 143% motor threshold) TMS of the left primary motor cortex at baseline and during intravenous midazolam administration. Single-pulse motor evoked potential (MEP) amplitude was used to assess corticospinal excitability. Short-interval paired-pulse responses were quantified as the ratio of conditioned to unconditioned MEP amplitude. At baseline, younger adults showed greater corticospinal excitability than older adults, reflected by larger single-pulse MEP amplitudes (adjusted p = 0.04). Younger adults demonstrated paired-pulse inhibition at baseline, reflected by a conditioned/unconditioned MEP ratio below 1.0 (ratio = 0.73; adjusted p < 0.01), whereas older adults did not show inhibition and instead had a mean ratio above 1.0 (ratio = 1.25). Midazolam reduced single-pulse MEP amplitudes in both groups. During midazolam administration, paired-pulse inhibition was no longer observed in younger adults, and older adults continued to show no evidence of inhibition. Younger and older adults differed in baseline corticospinal excitability and in short-interval paired-pulse TMS responses. Intravenous midazolam reduced corticospinal excitability and altered paired-pulse response patterns, eliminating baseline paired-pulse inhibition in younger adults while producing little measurable change in older adults. These findings suggest that aging may modify the net motor cortical response to benzodiazepine challenge. The results should be interpreted in relation to the paired-pulse stimulation parameters used and support further studies using complementary approaches to characterize age-related differences in inhibitory and facilitatory motor cortical circuits.

title: Cognitive correlates of diffusion tensor imaging analysis along the perivascular space index in amnestic mild cognitive impairment: a preliminary study.
journal: Archives of clinical neuropsychology : the official journal of the National Academy of Neuropsychologists
abstract: The diffusion tensor imaging analysis along the perivascular space (DTI-ALPS) index is an imaging-derived metric related to perivascular water diffusion and has been reported to correlate with global cognitive performance in dementia. However, its associations with specific cognitive functions in mild cognitive impairment (MCI) remain underexplored. This study aimed to characterize the cognitive correlates of the DTI-ALPS index in individuals with amnestic MCI. In this cross-sectional study, 57 participants with amnestic MCI underwent brain magnetic resonance imaging and a neuropsychological assessment battery. Correlations between the DTI-ALPS index and performance across the assessed cognitive measures were examined before and after adjustment for age, sex, education, and Fazekas score. Prior to adjustment, the DTI-ALPS index showed significant positive correlations with global cognitive measures, episodic memory retrieval, and semantic verbal fluency. After controlling for potential confounders, only the correlations with episodic memory and semantic verbal fluency remained significant. The DTI-ALPS index remained significantly associated with episodic memory retrieval and semantic verbal fluency in amnestic MCI after adjustment, suggesting a possible link with frontotemporal network-related cognitive functions. Further studies incorporating multimodal imaging and disease-specific biomarkers are warranted to clarify the biological significance of the DTI-ALPS index and its potential clinical relevance in early cognitive impairment.

title: Blood serotonin, ionized magnesium, cardiac troponin I, N-terminal pro-brain natriuretic peptide concentrations, and mitral valve billowing in horses with mitral valve regurgitation.
abstract: Serotonin, ionized magnesium (iMg), cardiac biomarkers, and mitral valve prolapse are extensively investigated in humans and dogs with mitral valve regurgitation (MR), but not in horses. To investigate serotonin, iMg, cardiac troponin I (cTnI), and N-terminal pro-brain natriuretic peptide (NT-proBNP) concentrations and degree of mitral valve billowing (MVB) in horses with MR. Eighty controls (no/trivial MR), 122 horses with MR (92 mild, 24 moderate, 6 severe). Prospective cross-sectional observational study. All horses underwent echocardiography with MVB distance assessment and MR classification. Platelet-poor plasma serotonin and serum iMg, cTnI, and NT-proBNP concentrations were determined. Controls and horses with different MR grades, biomarker concentrations, and MVB distance were compared using (non-)parametric tests. Ionized magnesium concentration was lower in MR compared to controls (mean difference, 0.03 mmol/L; 95% CI, 0.01-0.05; P = .01), but showed no correlation with billowing distance. The billowing distance was higher in horses with MR than in controls (septal: median difference, 0.2 cm; 95% CI, 0.1-0.3; P < .001; parietal: median difference, 0.3 cm; 95% CI, 0.2-0.3; P < .001), and in horses with a crescendo compared to a holosystolic MR jet (septal: median difference, 0.2 cm; 95% CI, 0.1-0.3; P = .003; parietal: median difference, 0.1 cm; 95% CI, 0.0-0.2; P = .01). No differences in serotonin, cTnI, and NT-proBNP concentrations were detected. Mitral valve billowing is to some extent likely physiological. The association of serotonin and iMg in MVB and MR requires further investigation. Both cTnI and NT-proBNP showed limited use as biomarkers of MR severity. Achtergrondinformatie: Serotonine, geïoniseerd magnesium (iMg), cardiale biomarkers en mitraalklep prolaps werden reeds uitgebreid onderzocht bij mensen en honden met mitraalklep regurgitatie (MR), in tegenstelling tot paarden met MR. Hypothese/Doelstelling: Het onderzoeken van de serotonine, iMg, cardiaal troponine I (cTnI) en N-terminal pro-brain natriuretic peptide (NT-proBNP) concentraties en de mate van bolling van de mitraalklep naar het linker atrium (MVB) bij paarden met MR. Studiepopulatie: Tachtig controle paarden (geen/triviaal MR), 122 paarden met MR (92 mild, 24 matig, 6 erg). Materiaal en methoden: Prospectieve cross-sectionele observationele studie. Alle paarden ondergingen echocardiografie, waarna de mate van MVB gemeten werd en MR classificatie uitgevoerd werd. De concentraties van serotonine in bloedplaatjesarm plasma en van iMg, cTnI en NT-proBNP in serum werden bepaald. Controle paarden en paarden met verschillende MR graden, biomarker concentraties en de mate van MVB werden onderling vergeleken aan de hand van (non-)parametrische testen. Resultaten: De concentratie iMg was lager bij paarden met MR in vergelijking met controle paarden (gemiddeld verschil, 0.03 mmol/L; 95% BI, 0.01-0.05; P = 0.01), maar vertoonde geen correlatie met de mate van MVB. De mate van MVB was hoger bij paarden met MR dan bij controle paarden (septaal: mediaan verschil, 0.2 cm; 95% BI, 0.1-0.3; P < 0.001; pariëtaal: mediaan verschil, 0.3 cm; 95% BI, 0.2-0.3; P < 0.001), en bij paarden met een crescendo MR jet in vergelijking met paarden met een holosystolische MR jet (septaal: mediaan verschil, 0.2 cm; 95% BI, 0.1-0.3; P = 0.003; pariëtaal: mediaan verschil, 0.1 cm; 95% BI, 0.0-0.2; P = 0.01). Er werden geen verschillen gedetecteerd in de concentraties van serotonine, cTnI en NT-proBNP. Conclusies en klinisch belang: De mate van MVB is tot op een bepaalde hoogte waarschijnlijk fysiologisch. De rol van serotonine en iMg in MVB en MR vergt verder onderzoek. Zowel cTnI als NT-proBNP vertoonden een beperkte meerwaarde als biomarkers bij het bepalen van de ernst van MR.

title: Clinical predictions using artificial intelligence in neurosurgery and its subspecialties: a systematic review and meta-analysis.
abstract: Artificial intelligence (AI) models for clinical prediction are proliferating across neurosurgery, but their aggregate discriminative performance, distribution along the care pathway and methodological quality are unclear. We systematically reviewed and meta-analysed these studies in neurosurgery and its subspecialities along with their risk of bias appraisal. We performed a PRISMA search on PubMed and Ovid for peer-reviewed original studies (2015-2026) using AI to predict a clinical outcome in neurosurgical populations. Metrics (primary- AUC; secondary- accuracy, sensitivity, specificity, c-index) were pooled using random effects modelling, overall, by subspeciality and care-pathway stage. Each study was classified as diagnostic, prognostic or forecasting and was assigned an evidence level. Clinical prediction task sub-stratification analysis was performed. Risk-of-bias was assessed using PROBAST. PROSPERO registered: CRD420261436614. 1063 studies were included. Across 451 (42.2%) studies reporting AUC, pooled discrimination was 0.86 (95% CI: 0.849-0.862), ranging from 0.84 (spine) to 0.87 (neuro-oncology), with extreme heterogeneity (I2 98.6%, τ2=0.27; 95% prediction interval: 0.68-0.94). Performance varied by clinical pathway stage, highest for diagnosis, grading and molecular tasks and lowest for post-operative tasks; pre-diagnosis, pre-operative and intra-operative applications were sparse, and treatment models were confined to neuro-oncology. Only 51 studies (4.8%) were using prospective data with external validation, whereas 619 (58%) rested on internal validation alone or no validation. 89% studies were at high risk-of-bias, driven by the analysis domain. Pooled discrimination was unchanged (AUC: 0.86%) when restricted to externally validated or non-high-risk studies. AI models report high performance across all the neurosurgical subspecialities, concordant across AUC, accuracy, sensitivity and specificity and robust to risk-of-bias stratification. Performance is highest for imaging-anchored diagnostic tasks and lowest at decision-facing post-operative stage. However, the literature is dominated by optimism-prone, internally-validated and poorly calibrated models with extreme heterogeneity. External validation, calibration analysis and reporting guidelines adherence remain prerequisites for clinical adoption.

title: Evaluation of the efficacy of Si-based agent in Rheumatoid Arthritis with complicating vestibular impairment.
abstract: Rheumatoid arthritis (RA) is a chronic autoimmune disease characterized by persistent joint inflammation and progressive disability. Although current therapies have improved clinical outcomes, safer and more effective therapeutic approaches remain needed. Silicon (Si)-based agents have antioxidant and anti-inflammatory properties and have shown beneficial effects in several inflammatory disease models. We evaluated the effects of oral administration of a Si-based agent in a type II collagen-induced arthritis mouse model. Arthritis severity was assessed using an arthritis index, hindlimb oedema, and the hindlimb extension reflex test. Serum type II collagen-specific autoantibody levels were also measured. Vestibular function was evaluated using the vestibulo-ocular reflex (VOR), and inner-ear structural changes were assessed by magnetic resonance imaging and histological analysis. The Si-based agent reduced arthritis-related outcomes, including the arthritis index, hindlimb oedema, and joint movement restriction, and reduced serum type II collagen-specific autoantibody levels. In contrast, no significant differences between the Si-based agent and control groups were detected in VOR-related outcomes, endolymphatic space measurements, or inner-ear histological findings. These findings suggest that the Si-based agent may have beneficial effects on arthritis-related manifestations. However, its effects on the vestibular function-related outcomes examined in this study were not evident. Further studies are needed to clarify the relationship between RA and vestibular dysfunction and to determine the potential therapeutic effects of Si-based agent on these complications.

title: Testing the effects of nicotine concentration and nicotine source claims on oral nicotine pouch packaging engagement, self-reported perceptions and use intentions, and product trial in young adults and adults: Protocol for a randomized trial.
abstract: Oral nicotine pouches (ONPs) are novel nicotine products and evidence on how features of ONP packaging affect product engagement, perceptions, use intentions, and behavior is limited. We outline the protocol for a randomized trial examining how nicotine concentration and nicotine source claims affect engagement with ONP packaging using psychophysiological measures, self-reported ONP perceptions and use intentions, and ONP trial (ClinicalTrials.gov: NCT06192316). Between 2024 and 2027, we will recruit 450 participants, comprised of: 150 young adults ages 18-24 who are susceptible but do not use tobacco; 150 young adults ages 18-24 who use tobacco; and 150 adults ages 25-65 who use tobacco. Participants complete procedures at an in-person laboratory visit. During the visit, participants complete pre-exposure self-report measures and are randomized between subjects to one of nine conditions in a 3 (Nicotine Concentration: None, Low, or High) x 3 (Nicotine Source Claim: None, Tobacco Free, or Synthetic) design. Within conditions, participants view 16 ONP pack images, in random order, reflecting different ONP brands and flavors. During exposure, we collect psychophysiological measures including heart rate, skin conductance, and visual attention. After exposure, participants complete self-report measures of ONP perceptions and use intentions, and a timed behavioral task where they are presented with ONP packages corresponding to their randomized condition and brands and flavors shown in the stimuli. Participants can try one of the products, and ONP trial is the behavioral outcome of interest. However, the packages do not contain ONPs; they contain commercially available pouches with food grade ingredients. At visit conclusion, participants are de-briefed and receive their incentive for participating. This project will generate evidence on the effects of nicotine concentration and source claims on ONP packaging in young adults who are not using but susceptible to tobacco, young adults using tobacco, and adults using tobacco to inform potential regulations.

title: The resource elasticity of control.
abstract: The ability to determine how much the environment can be controlled through our actions has long been viewed as fundamental to adaptive behavior. While traditional accounts treat controllability as a fixed property of the environment, we argue that real-world controllability often depends on the effort, time, and money we are able and willing to invest. In such cases, controllability can be said to be elastic to invested resources. Here, we propose that inferring this elasticity is essential for efficient resource allocation, and thus, elasticity misestimations result in maladaptive behavior. To test this hypothesis, we developed a novel treasure hunt game where participants encountered environments with varying degrees of controllability and elasticity. Across two pre-registered studies (N=514), we first demonstrate that people infer elasticity and adapt their resource allocation accordingly. We then present a computational model that explains how people make this inference and identify individual elasticity biases that lead to suboptimal resource allocation. Finally, we show that overestimation of elasticity is associated with elevated psychopathology involving an impaired sense of control. These findings establish the elasticity of control as a distinct cognitive construct guiding adaptive behavior and a computational marker for control-related maladaptive behavior.

title: Squalamine prevents motor and non-motor symptoms in the paraquat and lectin rat model of the body-first subtype of Parkinson's disease.
abstract: Increasing evidence supports the existence of a distinct body-first subtype of Parkinson's disease (PD), in which the initial site of pathology is in the gut. Animal models that recapitulate the body-first subtype of PD are needed. We tested the hypothesis that non-motor features of the body-first subtype of PD are recapitulated in the paraquat and lectin (P + L) rat model of PD, a model that has previously demonstrated the pathological motor progression of this subtype of PD. Then, we tested whether oral squalamine, a gastrointestinal prokinetic that has been shown to reduce formation of pathological α-synuclein, could prevent pathology, motor, and non-motor findings. Rats (n = 93) were orally gavaged for seven days with paraquat (1 mg/kg) and lectin (0.05%) in 1% sucrose solution. A subset of rats (n = 37) were given 30 days of squalamine (20 mg/kg) in their drinking water immediately following P + L treatment. Rats were tested for parkinsonian motor deficits, gastrointestinal dysmotility, sleep abnormalities, and cognitive deficits. Rats were euthanized and their brains processed for phospho-S129-α-synuclein pathology and neurodegeneration. We show that the P + L rat model recapitulates non-motor features and pathology of gastrointestinal dysmotility and sleep abnormalities seen in the body-first subtype of PD. We show that oral squalamine prevents motor deficits, gastrointestinal dysmotility, and sleep abnormalities, and diminishes phospho-S129-α-synuclein pathology and neurodegeneration in the nigrostriatal pathway. We show that the P + L rat model recapitulates many features of the body-first subtype of PD and provides pre-clinical evidence for the use of squalamine to mitigate progression in the body-first subtype of PD.

title: Atorvastatin inhibits PASMC proliferation in pulmonary hypertension via the TLR4/NF-κB/NLRP3/IL-1β pathway.
abstract: Pulmonary hypertension (PH) is a progressive disorder leading to right heart failure. This study explored how atorvastatin (ATO) alleviates PH using a multidisciplinary approach. Network pharmacology, molecular docking, and dynamics analysis were employed to identify ATO targets. A PH rat model was established via monocrotaline (40 mg/kg) subcutaneous injection, and animals were divided into CT, PH, and ATO (10 mg/kg/day) groups. Hemodynamics, histopathology, and immunofluorescence were evaluated. In vitro, pulmonary arterial smooth muscle cells (PASMCs) were exposed to PDGF-BB (20 ng/ml) with or without ATO (10-8 M). Cell proliferation was measured by CCK-8 and PCNA expression, and key proteins in the TLR4/NF-κB/NLRP3/IL-1β pathway were analyzed via western blot. siRNA-NLRP3 was used to verify NLRP3's role in PASMCs proliferation. Network pharmacology identified 277 common targets, with KEGG analysis linking ATO to the NF-κB signaling pathway. Docking showed strong binding affinity between ATO and TLR4 (-6.3 kCal/mol) through non-covalent interactions with ASN464 and PHE487. In vivo, ATO reduced right ventricular systolic pressure, right ventricular hypertrophy and pulmonary artery thickening. Immunofluorescence confirmed NLRP3 co-localization with α-SMA+ PASMCs. ATO downregulated TLR4/NF-κB/NLRP3/IL-1β protein expression in PH rats' lungs and PASMCs, and suppressed PDGF-BB-induced PASMCs proliferation via the pathway inhibition. Direct knockdown of NLRP3 reduced both PDGF-BB-induced and non-PDGF-BB-induced proliferation of PASMCs, and ATO primarily inhibited PASMCs proliferation through NLRP3. These findings demonstrate that ATO directly targets TLR4 to inhibit NF-κB/NLRP3/IL-1β signaling, thereby reducing PASMCs proliferation and suppressing PH progression.

title: Protocol for analyzing lncRNA-gene interactions in human fetal spinal cord development using single-cell and Stereo RNA sequencing.
abstract: Investigating changes in long noncoding RNA (lncRNA) and gene pairs across regions of the human fetal spinal cord offers crucial insights into human development. We present a protocol for analyzing lncRNA-gene pairs using 10× Visium Stereo RNA sequencing (Stereo-seq) and 10× Genomics single-cell RNA sequencing (scRNA-seq) data. We describe steps for collecting spinal cord tissues from gestational weeks 8 to 12, processing samples, and conducting sequencing analyses to explore cis and trans lncRNA regulatory interactions. For complete details on the use and execution of this protocol, please refer to Miao et al.1.

title: A shared multi-feature population code for sensory reliability across mouse visual cortex.
abstract: Successful behavior depends on evaluating both what is present in the environment and how reliable that information is. Yet how neural populations represent reliability, and whether this representation is shared across cortical areas, remains unknown. Using two-photon calcium imaging of over 150,000 neurons in mouse visual cortices during presentations of coherent motion stimuli, we find that sensory reliability is encoded through coordinated changes in response amplitude, selectivity, and signal-to-noise ratio. These coherence-dependent response patterns are not fully accounted for by stimulus-based normalization models; rather, they track the distribution of motion energy across directions, while remaining relatively invariant to total motion energy. This multi-feature code is expressed at the single-neuron and population levels and is consistent across visual areas, suggesting a shared encoding scheme rather than area-specific computations. Together, these findings support a common population code for stimulus reliability across visual cortices.

title: Semilunar nucleus neurons are highly excitable and potentiated by group I mGluRs to drive descending excitation to the mouse MNTB.
abstract: Medial nucleus of the trapezoid body (MNTB) neurons receive one of the largest synapses in the mammalian brain, the calyx of Held; however, multiple studies reported additional non-calyceal excitatory inputs of largely unresolved origin to MNTB neurons. Most recently, the semilunar nucleus (SLN) was identified as a potential source of such non-calyceal input in the rat. To elucidate the function of this novel pathway, we investigated the connectivity and physiology of the mouse SLN, with particular focus on neuromodulation by group I metabotropic glutamate receptors (mGluRs). Viral tracing not only confirmed the SLN-MNTB pathway in mice, but also revealed that MNTB-projecting SLN neurons received their input from the ipsilateral auditory cortex. Physiological characterization of SLN neurons using whole-cell patch-clamp recordings showed that SLN neurons, unlike most other auditory brainstem neurons, were intrinsically highly excitable. Electrical stimulation of the fibre tracts located dorsal to the SLN, evoked small, slow AMPA receptor-mediated EPSCs in SLN neurons that readily summated temporally. Immunolabeling revealed a heterogeneous expression of mGluR1 and mGluR5 across SLN neurons. A subpopulation of SLN neurons exhibited spontaneous action potential firing at resting membrane potential. Pharmacological activation of group I mGluRs further increased spontaneous firing of SLN neurons. Probing for functional connectivity between SLN and the ipsilateral MNTB, fibre tracts dorsal and lateral to the MNTB were stimulated, eliciting primarily non-calyceal AMPA receptor-mediated EPSCs in MNTB neurons. These findings suggest that SLN output may provide a glutamatergic tonic drive to MNTB neurons, potentially modulating their temporal processing. KEY POINTS: MNTB receives a descending input from the ipsilateral auditory cortex via SLN. SLN neurons are highly excitable during development and into maturation, with a subset exhibiting spontaneous firing at resting membrane potential. Descending glutamatergic input to SLN is small and slow, and shows consistent temporal summation. Group I mGluRs further enhance spontaneous firing of SLN neurons and both mGluR1 and mGluR5 are expressed in the SLN. Descending ipsilateral projections to MNTB neurons primarily drive glutamatergic, non-calyceal inputs.

title: Intuitive knowledge of object acoustics enables perceptual separation of physical variables from impact sounds.
journal: Proceedings of the National Academy of Sciences of the United States of America
abstract: Upon hearing objects collide, humans can estimate physical attributes such as material and mass. Although the physics of sound generation is well established, the inverse problem that listeners solve-of inferring physical parameters from sound-remains poorly understood. Classical accounts posit the use of acoustic cues that correlate with physical variables but do not explain how humans might distinguish multiple concurrent physical causes. To study this problem, we measured impulse responses from hundreds of everyday objects, extracted their resonances, and used statistics of the resonances to build a probabilistic generative model of impact sounds. We then used the model to synthesize and manipulate stimuli for experiments measuring judgments of physical variables. Humans accurately judged object properties from collision sounds. However, when both of the colliding objects varied, performance was impaired if the distribution of object resonances deviated from those measured in real-world objects. The results suggest that humans have internalized the statistical regularities of real-world object acoustics, and use this knowledge to separate the acoustic contributions of the distinct objects in the world that give rise to sounds.

title: Mussels possess distinct vanadium and iron storage systems for fabricating metal-reinforced adhesive fibers.
journal: Proceedings of the National Academy of Sciences of the United States of America
abstract: Mussels fashion a protein-based fibrous adhesive holdfast known as a byssus to tether themselves in marine habitats against crashing waves. The capacity of mussels to anchor securely is dependent on load-bearing protein-metal cross-links mediated by 3,4-dihydroxyphenylalanine (DOPA) residues coordinated to metal ions, which significantly enhance byssus mechanical properties (e.g., adhesive strength, abrasion resistance, toughness, self-healing capacity). However, the natural metal incorporation process during byssus formation remains poorly understood-a knowledge gap that limits the decades-old field of mussel-inspired materials from fulfilling its potential. Here, we investigate the natural byssus biofabrication system, the mussel foot, focusing specifically on iron and vanadium storage using a multilength scale ensemble of spectroscopic methods. Confocal Raman spectroscopy, synchrotron µ-X-ray fluorescence and µ-X-ray absorption spectroscopy, and scanning transmission electron microscopy with energy-dispersive X-ray spectroscopy studies indicate that these two metals occupy separate coordination environments: vanadium storage is DOPA-based, while iron is stored in ferritin-like structures. Lacking precedence, these findings indicate that mussels evolved a catechol-based metal storage system to specifically acquire and store what is typically considered a trace metal ion in biology, which they employ subsequently to mechanically reinforce protein-based glues and coatings produced by the mussel. Beyond the biological implications, these findings have potential to transform the field of mussel-inspired materials.

title: A thermosensitive bovine placenta decellularized extracellular matrix/Pluronic F127 composite hydrogel supports lineage specification and glia-associated development in hiPSC-derived human spinal cord organoids.
abstract: Human spinal cord organoids (hSCOs) provide valuable platforms for modeling spinal cord development, disease, and injury-related processes, but their maturation and cellular complexity remain strongly influenced by the culture matrix. Here, we developed a thermosensitive bovine placenta decellularized extracellular matrix/Pluronic F127 composite hydrogel (BP-dECM/PF127CH) as a cost-effective, ECM-rich three-dimensional matrix for the generation of hiPSC-derived hSCOs. The composite hydrogel exhibited a thermosensitive sol-gel transition at physiological temperature, an interconnected porous microarchitecture, and favorable cytocompatibility with hiPSCs, with levels of apoptosis, viability, and proliferation comparable to those observed with Matrigel. Under identical RA/SHH-based caudal-ventral induction conditions, BP-dECM/PF127CH-cultured hSCOs demonstrated significantly enhanced folding morphogenesis and, by Day 22, yielded 4.82-fold more NKX6.1+ ventral progenitors and 3.28-fold more PAX6+ cells comparable to Matrigel. This matrix-driven developmental reshaping resulted in 2.74-fold more HB9+ motor neurons, 2.19-fold more GFAP+ astrocytes, 1.29-fold more TMEM119+ microglia together with coordinated upregulation of VGLUT1 and GAD67 (1.55-fold each), indicating enhanced regional progenitor patterning, motor neuron differentiation, glial lineage diversification and balanced excitatory/inhibitory synaptic specification, while preserving global neuronal differentiation (Tuj1, MAP2) and myelination (MBP). With 99.62% DNA removal and retention of laminin and fibronectin, BP-dECM/PF127CH combines native ECM instructiveness with practical thermosensitive handling at 20-30-fold lower cost than Matrigel. This composite hydrogel establishes a versatile and scalable platform for engineering advanced organoid models with enhanced structural and cellular fidelity.

title: Drug Therapies and Incidence of Dementia Among Adults With Overactive Bladder.
abstract: Concern that anticholinergic medications for overactive bladder (OAB) are associated with increased dementia risk has encouraged a shift toward β3 adrenergic agonists, which are presumed cognitively safer. Whether this presumption is justified is uncertain. To compare the risk of incident dementia among adults initiating high-risk anticholinergic, low-risk anticholinergic, or β3 agonist therapy for OAB and to evaluate the association of treatment duration with risk. This retrospective cohort study used Epic Cosmos electronic health record data from 2012 to 2025. Adults aged 40 to 90 years newly treated for OAB within 1 year of diagnosis without preexisting dementia were included. First prescribed medication class: high-risk anticholinergics (oxybutynin, tolterodine, or solifenacin), low-risk anticholinergics (darifenacin, trospium, or fesoterodine), or β3 agonists (mirabegron or vibegron). Incident dementia by diagnosis code or dementia-specific medication. Inverse probability of treatment weighting (IPTW) and Cox proportional hazards models were used, with analyses stratified by age and sex and an exploratory landmark duration-response analysis. Among 830 393 patients (585 198 female [70.5%]; median [IQR] age, 67 [57-76] years), incident dementia occurred in 65 134 patients, with a median (IQR) follow-up ranging from 1046 (571-1809) days for β3 agonists to 1568 (857-2614) days for high-risk anticholinergics. After IPTW, high-risk anticholinergics were associated with a lower hazard of dementia than β3 agonists (hazard ratio [HR], 0.90; 95% CI, 0.87-0.93) and low-risk anticholinergics (HR, 0.93; 95% CI, 0.90-0.96); low-risk anticholinergics did not differ from β3 agonists (HR, 0.97; 95% CI, 0.93-1.01). Weighted 10-year dementia risk was highest for β3 agonists (20.0%; 95% CI, 18.8%-21.2%) and lowest for high-risk anticholinergics (18.1%; 95% CI, 17.9%-18.3%). E-values of 1.29 (high-risk anticholinergics vs β3 agonists) and 1.20 (high-risk vs low-risk anticholinergics) suggested that observed differences could be explained by a modest amount of unmeasured confounding. Longer anticholinergic duration was not associated with increased risk. In this cohort study of patients undergoing treatment for OAB, β3 agonists were not associated with a lower dementia incidence compared with anticholinergics. These findings suggest that previously reported increases in risk may reflect residual confounding rather than a pharmacological effect.

title: Guillain-Barré Syndrome Following Bariatric Surgery: A Systematic Literature Review.
abstract: This systematic review aims to characterize the clinical features, associated micronutrient deficiencies, and outcomes of Guillain-Barré syndrome (GBS) following bariatric surgery, and to examine the potential mechanisms linking bariatric procedures to GBS development. We conducted a systematic literature review of the PubMed, Google Scholar, and Web of Science databases to identify adult GBS cases in patients who had undergone bariatric surgery, published between January 2002 and January 2023. The review was conducted in accordance with PRISMA guidelines and complemented by data from our institutional bariatric surgery registry. 35 adult patients with GBS were identified after bariatric surgery, including 2 cases from our hospital registry. A literature review revealed 33 published cases, primarily following sleeve gastrectomy. Neurological deficits included motor weakness, sensory deficits, cranial nerve dysfunction, and autonomic dysfunction. Significant deficiencies in vitamins B1, B6, B12, and E were noted. Intravenous immunoglobulin was administered to 54.3% of patients. Complete recovery was observed in 45.7% of patients. This review identifies an association rather than a causal relationship between bariatric surgery and GBS. Nutritional deficiencies and immune dysregulation following surgery may act as contributing factors in susceptible individuals; however, a direct causal link remains unestablished. Clinicians should maintain heightened awareness of this complication and ensure timely neurological assessment in bariatric surgery patients presenting with new neurological symptoms.

title: Pharmacological Management of Atrial Fibrillation Across the Heart Failure Ejection Fraction Spectrum: Rate Control, Rhythm Control, and Beyond.
abstract: To summarise the contemporary pharmacological management of atrial fibrillation (AF) in heart failure (HF), focusing on rate and rhythm control and upstream therapies across the ejection fraction spectrum. Rate control remains a cornerstone of AF management, particularly in permanent AF or haemodynamically fragile patients, with beta-blockers, digoxin, and non-dihydropyridine calcium channel blockers selected according to ejection fraction phenotype. Concurrently, increasing evidence supports early rhythm-control strategies because of their prognostic benefits in HF populations, with current guidelines reinforcing a left ventricular ejection fraction (LVEF)-guided approach to antiarrhythmic drug selection. Beyond conventional drugs, HF guideline-directed medical therapy (GDMT) is emerging as an important upstream pharmacological strategy for modulation of the arrhythmogenic substrate. AF management in HF requires an integrated, phenotype-oriented approach combining symptom control, thromboembolic prevention, and optimisation of GDMT. LVEF remains a key determinant of pharmacological safety and therapeutic selection, whereas haemodynamic status primarily guides acute management decisions.

title: Impact of Particulate Matter Exposure on Neurological Health in Older Adults: A Systematic Review.
abstract: This systematic review evaluates the current epidemiological evidence on the relationship between particulate matter (PM) exposure and neurological health in older adults, with particular attention to cognitive decline and neurodegenerative disease. A PRISMA-guided systematic search of PubMed, Scopus, Web of Science, and ScienceDirect was conducted through January 2026. Twenty-one observational studies met the inclusion criteria. The most frequently studied outcomes were cognitive performance and decline and cognitive impairment, including mild cognitive impairment (MCI), with several studies reporting adverse associations, particularly for long-term PM2.5 exposure. Evidence for dementia and Alzheimer's disease was also provided by several large cohort studies, although findings varied across exposure metrics and clinical endpoints. In contrast, evidence for Parkinson's disease-related hospitalizations, cerebral amyloid burden, retinal neurodegeneration, mental disorder-related hospital admissions, and individual PM constituents was more limited and was often based on one or a few studies. Findings concerning specific PM constituents were heterogeneous and should therefore be considered exploratory. The available evidence suggests an association between PM exposure and adverse neurological health in older adults, with the most substantial evidence concerning long-term PM2.5 exposure and cognitive outcomes. However, the strength and certainty of the evidence vary considerably across pollutants and neurological endpoints. Heterogeneity in study design, exposure assessment, and outcome definitions should be considered when interpreting the overall findings.

title: Temporally evolving neuronal remodeling via the CTNNB1-NRG3-ERBB4 axis drives therapy resistance in glioblastoma.
abstract: Glioblastoma (GBM) remains highly lethal despite early therapeutic responses, as resistance inevitably emerges. While clinical studies show improvements in progression-free survival (PFS) during the early response (ER) phase, the molecular trajectory bridging ER and recurrent resistance (RR)-and the adaptive resistance programs temporally engaged during this transition- remain poorly understood. To dissect the dynamic molecular evolution underlying therapy resistance, patient-derived xenograft (PDX) models were treated with anti-VEGF therapy. Longitudinal proteogenomic profiling across multiple time points was performed to capture time-resolved molecular changes associated with the tumor response to the therapy. Longitudinal analyses revealed a dynamic, temporally evolving response trajectory, with an initial response phase (IRP) marked by neuronal-like remodeling, and a late response phase (LRP) characterized by mesenchymal transdifferentiation and metabolic adaptation. Proteomic and phosphoproteomic analyses identified the CTNNB1-NRG3-ERBB4 signaling axis as a key driver of neuronal-like remodeling during the IRP. Mechanistically, β-catenin activation upregulated NRG3, promoting postsynaptic scaffold remodeling, while pharmacological inhibition of β-catenin/CBP with PRI-724 disrupted this neuronal program and significantly extended survival in vivo. These findings place neuronal-like remodeling within a time-resolved framework of tumor adaptation to anti-VEGF therapy in GBM and highlight the CTNNB1-NRG3-ERBB4 axis as a tractable therapeutic target, providing a rationale for combination strategies to overcome anti-VEGF therapy failure.

title: Combination of ezetimibe and sericin attenuates cadmium chloride-induced neurotoxicity in an experimental rat model by suppressing oxidative stress and neuroinflammation.
abstract: Cadmium chloride (CdCl2)-induced neurotoxicity is a global health concern, associated with oxidative stress, neuroinflammation, and downregulation of IGF-1R/GLP-1R/Nrf2/HO-1 signaling pathway. Agents targeting this pathway may offer a promising strategy to mitigate neurotoxic effects.
