title: An approximation of MRI R2* as a rapid surrogate of nigral iron in Parkinson's disease.
abstract: Nigral iron accumulation is a robust imaging marker of Parkinson's disease and is commonly assessed using R2* mapping. However, its clinical implementation is limited by long acquisition times. An alternative metric, effective R2, derived from dual-contrast proton density- and T2-weighted MRI, has recently been proposed as a fast surrogate of tissue iron content. Using data from the Parkinson's Progression Markers Initiative (PPMI), we evaluated the diagnostic and longitudinal performance of effective R2 in the substantia nigra (SN) across multiple scanner platforms. Cross-sectional analysis demonstrated significantly higher effective R2 values in de novo Parkinson's disease patients (n=187) compared with prodromal subjects (n=26), with consistent effects across acquisition protocols. In Siemens data (177 patients and 25 prodromal subjects), effective R2 achieved good discriminative performance for Parkinson's disease classification (AUC = 0.85). Longitudinal analysis for 14 patients over 36 months showed no significant change in effective R2 values despite clinical progression measured by MDS-UPDRS Part III scores. These findings indicate that effective R2 provides robust cross-sectional discrimination of early Parkinson's disease but with limited sensitivity to disease progression.

title: Genetically predicted cocaine addiction vulnerability is associated with elevated GABAergic transmission in the central amygdala of drug-naïve rats.
abstract: A central unresolved question in addiction neuroscience is whether the cellular differences that distinguish vulnerable from resilient individuals precede drug exposure or arise as its consequence. Because addiction-like phenotypes are conventionally assigned only after drug exposure, existing evidence cannot readily separate predisposition from neuroadaptation. Here we used RATTACA, a genome-wide prediction method developed for heterogeneous stock (HS) rats, to select drug-naïve rats with high or low genetically predicted cocaine addiction severity and characterized synaptic transmission by whole-cell recording before any drug exposure, in three independent cohorts. Rats with a high predicted addiction severity showed elevated spontaneous inhibitory postsynaptic current (sIPSC) frequency in the medial subdivision of the central amygdala (CeM), and sIPSC frequency scaled continuously with the predicted severity across rats. Amplitude and kinetics were unchanged, a pattern consistent with greater presynaptic GABAergic input. In separate cohorts, GABAergic transmission in the nucleus accumbens core (NAc core) and glutamatergic transmission in the CeM did not differ between groups, suggesting that, among the measures examined, the association was specific to CeM inhibitory transmission. Bath-applied cocaine reduced CeM sIPSC frequency by a similar proportion in both groups and increased CeM glutamatergic transmission. Because high-predicted rats started from a higher baseline, the absolute reduction in spontaneous inhibitory input was larger in these rats. Groups did not differ in locomotor activity. These findings identify elevated spontaneous GABAergic transmission in the CeM as a pre-existing correlate of polygenic cocaine addiction risk and show that genome-wide prediction can dissociate innate cellular predisposition from drug-induced adaptation.

title: When colours speak: context-dependent chromatic expression during predation in Sepia (acanthosepion) pharaonis.
abstract: Predator-prey encounters constitute high-risk events for both interacting parties. These encounters are accompanied by changes in internal state, notably through increased arousal. Although cephalopods are renowned for their dynamic body patterns, the extent to which these chromatic displays track internal arousal or emotional valence during predation remains largely unresolved. We investigated seven chromatic components expressed by five subadults Sepia (acanthosepion) pharaonis (Ehrenberg, 1831) under controlled variations of prey accessibility, social context, and hunting outcomes to determine whether body-pattern dynamics reflect underlying emotion-like states. Chromatic expression intensified as predation progressed, peaking when prey was held in the arms. This rise was dominated by the Fragmented dark mantle component, which could serve as a potential marker of increased arousal. In contrast, one component - red fins, was selectively upregulated in situations with presumed negative valence, including inaccessible prey or the presence of a conspecific. Papillate skin expression decreased during prey capture, with papillae becoming less prominent at the moment of prey seizure, potentially contributing to improved hydrodynamic efficiency. Together, these findings provide the first evidence that S. pharaonis cuttlefish exhibits context-dependent, dissociable chromatic signatures during prey capture. These differences are consistent with the expression of arousal and valence. Our work offers a quantitative framework for interpreting cephalopod body patterns as indicators of internal states and informs broader theories on the evolution of emotional expression in non-human animals.

title: Evaluation of Zebrafish (Danio rerio) as a Potential Experimental Host for Rhinosporidium seeberi Under Laboratory Exposure Conditions.
abstract: Rhinosporidiosis is a chronic granulomatous disease caused by Rhinosporidium seeberi, an aquatic pathogen whose life cycle and host interactions remain poorly understood due to the absence of an in vitro culture system and a reliable experimental animal model. Phylogenetic placement of R. seeberi within the Mesomycetozoea and its strong association with fresh water habitats suggest a possible role for aquatic vertebrates as alternative or intermediate hosts. In this study, we evaluated whether zebrafish (Danio rerio) could serve as a potential experimental host for R. seeberi. Adult zebrafish were exposed to histopathologically, and PCR confirmed human rhinosporidiosis tissue under passive immersion and trauma-enhanced conditions and monitored for up to 90 days post-exposure (dpe). Behavioural activity, feeding, survival, and gross morphology were assessed longitudinally, followed by quantitative behavioural analysis and whole-fish histopathology. Zebrafish exhibited no mortality, signs of infection, behavioural abnormalities, or external lesions throughout the study period. Quantitative locomotor analysis revealed no infection-associated behavioural changes. Histopathological examination of major organs, including gills, liver, muscle, kidney, stomach, heart and brain, revealed no evidence of R. seeberi sporangia, endospores, granulomatous inflammation, or tissue pathology at either 30 or 90 dpe. These findings indicate that R. seeberi has a limited potential to infect zebrafish under laboratory exposure conditions. This study provides the first experimental evidence that zebrafish are unlikely to serve as a model for rhinosporidiosis and underscores the need to explore alternative hosts and experimental approaches to investigate the biology of this uncultivable pathogen.

title: ACOD1-itaconate axis activation attenuates coagulopathy and improves neurological outcomes after traumatic brain injury by suppressing neutrophil extracellular trap formation.
abstract: Coagulopathy following traumatic brain injury (TBI) exacerbates secondary neurodegeneration and increases mortality. Neutrophil infiltration and neutrophil extracellular trap (NET) formation are strongly implicated in this post-TBI coagulopathy, suggesting that NET suppression may improve clinical outcome. The immunometabolite itaconate, generated via aconitate decarboxylase 1 (ACOD1), possesses documented anti-inflammatory and cytoprotective properties, but effects on NET formation and coagulopathy post-TBI are largely unexplored. This study examined if the ACOD1-itaconate metabolic pathway serves as an endogenous checkpoint to restrain NET formation, whether ACOD1-itaconate axis dysregulation contributes to coagulopathy and poor outcome following TBI, and if targeting this axis could be a viable therapeutic strategy. A retrospective analysis of the MIMIC-IV database was performed to compare outcomes between TBI patients with and without coagulopathy. Culture and mouse model experiments were conducted to assess the impact of NETs on endothelial cell phenotype and cerebral microcirculation. Single-cell RNA sequencing and pharmacological studies of cultured neutrophils and model mice were employed to investigate the effects of the ACOD1-itaconate axis on NET formation and neurological outcome. Retrospective analysis revealed more severe hypoxia and higher mortality in coagulopathic TBI patients. In coculture and TBI model mice, NETs promoted a procoagulant endothelial phenotype and exacerbated microthrombosis. Hypoxia suppressed the ACOD1-itaconate axis in neutrophils, relieving endogenous inhibition on NET formation. Exogenous 4-OI administration rescued this defect, significantly suppressing NET formation, restoring coagulation function, and mitigating secondary brain injury and neurological deficits in mice. The ACOD1-itaconate pathway is a crucial metabolic checkpoint that restrains NET activity, while suppression post-TBI facilitates pathological NET formation, driving coagulopathy and secondary injury. These findings identify components of the ACOD1-itaconate-NET axis as novel therapeutic targets for treating TBI-induced coagulopathy.

title: Interhemispheric structural connectivity alterations and hierarchical connectome gradient reorganization following SARS-CoV-2 infection.
abstract: Neurological sequelae of SARS-CoV-2 infection extend beyond the acute phase, yet the structural basis of network-level brain changes across disease severity remains poorly understood. We investigated structural brain connectivity and connectome gradient organization in adults with polymerase chain reaction-confirmed coronavirus disease 2019 (COVID-19), stratified into non-hospitalized and hospitalized groups, alongside a comparison group with non-COVID respiratory infection, using 3T diffusion-weighted magnetic resonance imaging. Network-Based Statistics was used to identify subnetworks of altered structural connectivity, and connectome gradients were derived separately for each hemisphere using diffusion map embedding and compared across groups within seven canonical resting-state networks. Network-Based Statistics identified a predominantly interhemispheric subnetwork differing across the three groups, linking left-hemispheric control and salience regions to right hemisphere sensory and association areas, with a related subnetwork distinguishing hospitalized participants from the comparison group. Connectome gradient analysis revealed group-related differences in connectivity-derived embedding positions within sensorimotor and dorsal attention networks, more pronounced among hospitalized participants. These findings suggest that SARS-CoV-2 infection is associated with severity-related interhemispheric structural connectivity differences and altered hierarchical connectome organization, particularly within sensorimotor and dorsal attentional systems. Given the cross-sectional design, modest sample size, and absence of behavioral data, these findings should be considered exploratory and do not establish anatomical fiber loss, causal mechanisms, or predictive clinical value; instead, they provide a structural framework to guide future studies of neurological outcomes after COVID-19.

title: Mechanism by which metformin alleviates neuralgia in the spinal cord of diabetic rats.
abstract: Painful diabetic neuropathy (PDN) is a common chronic complication of diabetes mellitus (DM). Metformin is a widely used hypoglycemic drug that exerts anti-inflammatory and antioxidant effects. In the present study, we revealed that metformin attenuates mechanical allodynia through the AMPK pathway in the spinal cord of DM rats. Metformin intervention significantly elevated the levels of phosphorylated-AMPK (p-AMPK, the activated form of AMPK) in the L4-6 spinal dorsal horn (SDH) of DM rats. In addition, the inhibition of AMPK activation by Compound C clearly blocked metformin-mediated analgesia. Moreover, AICAR treatment significantly attenuated mechanical allodynia. Additionally, AMPK activation was observed in both neurons and glial cells. Interestingly, metformin intervention reduced the activation levels of microglia and astrocytes in the L4-6 SDH of DM rats, which suggests that AMPK plays a complicated role at the cellular level in the spinal cord. In conclusion, metformin alleviates diabetic mechanical allodynia by activating AMPK signaling in the L4-6 SDH of DM rats, and inhibits microglial and astrocytic activation. These findings support the potential use of metformin in the clinical treatment of PDN.

title: Narrowing margins: exploring how MeCP2 deficiency degrades precision, timing, and adaptability in motor circuits.
abstract: The X-linked gene methyl-CpG-binding protein 2 (MECP2) is a critical epigenetic regulator with important roles in neuronal gene regulation and neuronal plasticity during sensitive periods of development and beyond. Mutations in MECP2 result in Rett syndrome (RTT), a neurodevelopmental disorder predominantly affecting females. Motor dysfunction is among the most consistently disrupted domains in RTT. The literature on this domain is under-synthesized and a cohesive framework to explain the neurobiological underpinnings of the varied motor phenotypes by sex, allele and age is lacking. In this review, we focus on the literature on motor dysfunction in RTT and propose a convergent-constraint model, in which MeCP2 loss compromises mitochondrial capacity, GPCR signaling, and calcium handling in high-energy-demand neuronal populations, with perineuronal nets acting as a structural node that reinforces this constraint. This model accounts for a recurring pattern across the intervention literature: genetic, viral, pharmacological, and behavioral approaches consistently produce partial, overlapping rescue rather than full correction, consistent with circuits operating below capacity rather than missing a single essential component. We identify testable hypotheses and gaps in the field, including the temporal sequence of these constraints and the absence of motor-specific mechanistic data for current and emerging therapies, that offer potential avenues for combinatorial therapeutic targets for RTT.

title: From NAD+ elevation to clinical benefit: tissue-specific regulation and translational barriers in aging and age-related disease.
abstract: Nicotinamide adenine dinucleotide (NAD+) decline has been implicated in aging and age-related disease, and precursor supplementation with nicotinamide riboside (NR) or nicotinamide mononucleotide (NMN) has shown efficacy in preclinical models. Human trials, however, have produced inconsistent functional outcomes, and the sources of this translational gap remain poorly defined. We combined a bibliometric analysis of 3,271 aging-focused NAD+ publications (2004-2025) with a critical synthesis of mechanistic and clinical evidence to localize where and why preclinical findings fail to translate. The bibliometric analysis revealed three structural features of the literature: (i) original research articles dominated the corpus, whereas the document-type classification cannot distinguish preclinical experiments from human observational or interventional studies; (ii) research is siloed across disease domains with limited cross-tissue comparison; and (iii) intervention-oriented keywords (NMN, NR, supplementation, drug delivery) have outpaced empirical clinical validation. Mechanistic synthesis showed that these structural gaps correspond to biological heterogeneity: NAD+ biosynthesis, consumption, redox balance, and subcellular compartmentalization are tissue- and compartment-specific, such that systemic precursor elevation does not uniformly restore functional NAD+ in disease-relevant tissues. Four subcellular pools-nuclear, cytosolic, mitochondrial, and axonal-each possess distinct rate-limiting bottlenecks, and hepatic metabolic reserve introduces an overlooked source of inter-individual variability. Across neurodegeneration, metabolic disease, cardiovascular aging, and sarcopenia, NAD+ dysregulation follows disease-specific mechanisms rather than a universal decline phenotype. We propose a precision-medicine framework that shifts the core question from whether NAD+ can be elevated to whether a defined intervention corrects a specific NAD+ defect in the appropriate tissue and subcellular compartment. This framework provides a structured basis for designing next-generation NAD+-targeted trials with tissue-specific biomarkers and function-oriented endpoints.

title: Comprehensive vaccination guidelines for patients with inborn errors of immunity: A European Society for Immunodeficiencies Consensus.
journal: The Journal of allergy and clinical immunology
abstract: Inborn errors of immunity (IEI) encompass over 550 subtypes characterized by impaired immune responses. Individuals with IEI may exhibit suboptimal vaccination immune responses, and some risk severe adverse events following live attenuated vaccines. The International Union of Immunological Societies (IUIS) categorizes IEIs into 10 groups based on most consistently reported phenotypes. Previous vaccination recommendations lack IEI subtype-specific guidance aligned with IUIS classification, limiting clinical utility in daily practice. To develop comprehensive, tailored vaccination recommendations for distinct IEI subgroups based on specific immune defects, vaccine types, therapeutic regimens, and exposure risks. An expert panel collaborated with the European Society for Immunodeficiencies (ESID) Clinical Working Party to develop evidence-based guidelines, with consensus defined as ≥75% expert agreement on contested recommendations. The guidelines incorporate the IUIS 2024 classification and address individual risk assessment based on IEI subtype, vaccine type, and treatment regimen. Non-live vaccines are safe for all IEI patients but provide varying protection depending on the underlying disorder. Live attenuated vaccines are contraindicated in many IEI subtypes, though individual assessment may permit exceptions. Influenza and pneumococcal vaccines are strongly recommended given patients' respiratory infections vulnerability. Novel recommendations include tick-borne encephalitis and SARS-CoV-2 vaccines, treatment-specific approaches, and travel advice. These ESID guidelines provide IEI subtype-specific vaccination recommendations, enabling personalized approaches that optimize protection while minimizing adverse event risks.

title: Phytocannabinoids in neurologic, neuropsychiatric, inflammatory, pain, cardiometabolic, hepatic, renal, and neoplastic disorders: Pharmacology, clinical evidence, and translational perspectives.
abstract: Phytocannabinoids are pharmacologically diverse constituents of Cannabis sativa whose actions go beyond canonical cannabinoid receptors. Δ9-Tetrahydrocannabinol (THC) and cannabidiol (CBD) are best characterized, while cannabigerol, cannabidivarin, tetrahydrocannabivarin, cannabichromene, cannabinol, and related compounds are emerging candidates. This review integrates molecular pharmacology, pharmacokinetics, safety, and therapeutic evidence across neurologic, neuropsychiatric, inflammatory, pain, cardiovascular and metabolic, hepatic, renal, and neoplastic disorders. The strongest evidence supports pharmaceutical-grade oral CBD as adjunctive therapy for seizures associated with Dravet syndrome, Lennox-Gastaut syndrome, and tuberous sclerosis complex, and standardized THC-CBD formulations for selected patients with multiple sclerosis-associated spasticity. Emerging clinical signals in schizophrenia, pain, fibromyalgia, sleep disturbance, substance-use disorders, dermatologic conditions, sickle cell disease, and other symptom-focused indications support continued development. However, efficacy remains compound-, formulation-, exposure-, and indication-specific. In oncology, supportive-care applications must remain distinct from tumor-directed treatment, for which clinical efficacy has not been established. Preclinical studies show coherent effects on neuronal excitability, glial and immune activation, endothelial dysfunction, oxidative and nitrative stress, mitochondrial injury, fibrosis, and regulated cell death. These findings support further investigation in neurodegeneration, ischemia-reperfusion injury, diabetic cardiovascular disease, immune-mediated disorders, hepatic and renal injury, and selected cancers. Translation is constrained by product heterogeneity, variable exposure, uncertain target engagement, model differences, drug interactions, and underpowered trials. Standardized products, exposure-informed dosing, pharmacodynamic biomarkers, responder-enriched designs, and indication-specific randomized studies can address these barriers. Phytocannabinoids therefore represent a promising therapeutic platform whose potential will be best realized by matching defined compounds and formulations to biologically coherent diseases, mechanisms, treatment windows, and patient populations.

title: Propionate, a short-chain fatty acid, is associated with disease activity in pediatric-onset multiple sclerosis.
abstract: Short-chain fatty acids (SCFAs), metabolites found in fermented foods and produced by colonic bacterial fermentation of dietary fibers, may mediate gut-brain axis crosstalk influencing the course of multiple sclerosis (MS). In this study, SCFAs are measured in plasma and paired stool samples by targeted mass spectrometry in a large cohort of deeply phenotyped individuals shortly after MS onset. Propionate is consistently associated with a protective effect on three clinical and imaging activity-related outcomes. Findings are reproduced in an equally large external cohort for plasma and stool measurements. Despite the correlation between plasma SCFAs and SCFA-producing gut microbial taxa, propionate levels are not correlated with dietary fiber, suggesting that intake may not be sufficient to modulate its levels and ensuing inflammation. In conclusion, propionate is consistently associated with lower disease activity, and exogenous administration may be more likely than fiber supplementation to confer protective effects on MS activity in proof-of-concept clinical trials.

title: Validation of the Scottish epilepsy deaths study (SEDS) score using routinely collected data in Wales: a retrospective cohort study.
abstract: The Scottish Epilepsy Deaths Study (SEDS) Score was developed to identify individuals at increased risk of epilepsy-related death. We externally validated the SEDS Score within the Welsh Population using the Secure Anonymised Information Linkage (SAIL) databank. This is a retrospective cohort study of adults (≥18 years) with epilepsy living in Wales, 2015-2019. Five annual cohorts were created, with individuals followed for one year. Epilepsy-related deaths were defined as deaths with epilepsy recorded on death certificates. SEDS Scores were calculated for all individuals at the beginning of each cohort year and used to categorise low, medium, high, and very-high risk groups based on individual SEDS Scores. We used logistic regression to compare odds-ratios (ORs) for epilepsy-related death in each of the SEDS Score risk groups. We found 423 epilepsy-related deaths amongst 117,724 epilepsy person-years. An increasing SEDS Score was associated with increasing risk of epilepsy-related death. Odds ratios (95% confidence intervals) for epilepsy-related deaths within one year (compared to the reference category (SEDS Score = 0)) for low, medium, high and very high-risk SEDS Score categories were 4.5 (1.6-10.0); 1.3 (1.0-1.7); 3.2 (2.4-4.3); and 7.6 (5.6-10.4) respectively. The SEDS Score demonstrates predictive value in identifying individuals at higher risk of epilepsy-related death within the Welsh population. SEDS Score performed particularly well for the high and very high-risk categories and may help prioritise targeted preventative interventions.

title: Structural brain age trajectories in antipsychotic-naive first episode psychosis.
abstract: Psychotic disorders such as schizophrenia have been associated with older-appearing brain structure, commonly quantified using the brain-age paradigm. However, it remains unclear whether these alterations are present at illness onset and whether antipsychotic treatment modifies their trajectory. In this study, 61 (28 females and 33 males) antipsychotic-naïve people with first-episode psychosis were randomized to receive either a second-generation antipsychotic (risperidone or paliperidone) or placebo over a 6-month treatment period, alongside intensive psychosocial therapy. A healthy control group (n = 27, 17 females, 10 males) was also recruited. Structural MRI scans were collected at baseline, 3 months, and 12 months. Brain age was estimated using two pretrained and validated models (Pyment and CentileBrain). Brain-predicted age difference (brain-PAD) did not differ between patients and healthy controls at baseline (F(1,80) = 0.81, p = 0.37). There were also no significant effects of time, treatment group (antipsychotic, placebo, healthy control), or their interaction on brain-PAD across the first year (all p > 0.26). Findings were consistent across both brain-age models, and brain-PAD was not associated with clinical and lifestyle measures. These findings suggest that altered structural brain aging is not evident during the earliest stages of psychosis and is not modified by early antipsychotic exposure over the first year of illness. Longer follow-up and approaches that account for illness heterogeneity may be needed to clarify when brain-age alterations emerge in psychotic disorders. Australian New Zealand Clinical Trials Registry (http://www.anzctr.org.au/; ACTRN12607000608460).

title: Paradoxical ethnic differences in prevalence of vascular risk factors versus extracranial atherosclerotic disease in TIA/stroke patients in the United Kingdom: Population-based study and meta-analysis.
abstract: Studies in Northern America report a lower prevalence of coronary artery disease (CAD) in Black than White people despite higher prevalence of vascular risk factors. However, it remains unclear to what extent these differences are driven by biology or reflect ethnic disparities in smoking, socioeconomic deprivation, healthcare access, and health-seeking behaviour. We aimed to determine if ethnic differences in coronary and peripheral artery disease persist in people with stroke living in the United Kingdom (UK), considering that most people with stroke seek medical attention and the National Health Service provides equitable access to care. In a prospective population-based cohort of all patients with suspected TIA or stroke in Oxfordshire, UK (Oxford Vascular Study, OxVasc, April 2002 to March 2023), we fitted multivariable logistic regression models to quantify the association of ethnicity and extracranial atherosclerotic disease (coronary or peripheral) while adjusting for age, sex, vascular risk factors, and socioeconomic deprivation. We verified our findings in a systematic review of UK-based studies reporting prevalence of extracranial atherosclerotic disease and associated vascular risk factors across ethnic groups. Prevalence estimates were pooled by random-effects meta-analysis. In 7297 OxVasc participants (52.6% women, 71.0 ± 15.5 years), non-White people (n = 335) had a higher prevalence of diabetes mellitus (OR = 3.26, 2.55-4.16). However, Black people had a lower prevalence of CAD (OR = 0.31, 0.10-0.98, p = 0.046) or any extracranial atherosclerotic disease (OR = 0.42, 0.18-0.96, p = 0.04) than White people. After adjustment for age, sex, vascular risk factors, and deprivation, the difference was attenuated both for CAD (aOR = 0.50, 0.18-1.41, p = 0.19) and any extracranial atherosclerotic disease (aOR = 0.43, 0.18-1.04, p = 0.06). Asian and White people had similar prevalence of CAD and extracranial atherosclerotic disease. Among UK-based studies of patients with stroke, Black and Asian people were more likely than White people to have diabetes (pooled OR: 2.78, 2.40-3.22, n = 3 studies; 4.15, 3.11-5.53 n = 6), hypertension (1.95, 1.47-2.60, n = 3; 1.47, 1.02-2.12, n = 6), and obesity (1.52, 1.27-1.83, n = 1; 1.2, 0.66-2.29, n = 3) but less likely to be smoking (0.70, 0.50-0.97, n = 2; 0.57, 0.44-0.74, n = 5). Yet, Black people had less CAD than White (0.48, 0.31-0.76, n = 3) and Asian (0.30, 0.10-0.80, n = 2) people. We confirm the existence of a coronary artery disease paradox in Black but not Asian people with TIA or stroke, which is likely independent of biases in healthcare access or health-seeking behaviour, and may suggest different biological susceptibilities.

title: Disrupted cortical signatures of response inhibition in Parkinson's disease revealed by TMS-EEG.
journal: Clinical neurophysiology : official journal of the International Federation of Clinical Neurophysiology
abstract: Inhibitory control deficits are a hallmark of Parkinson's disease (PD), particularly in patients with L-DOPA-induced dyskinesias (LID), but the cortical mechanisms underlying impaired inhibition remain poorly understood. We used transcranial magnetic stimulation and electroencephalography (TMS-EEG) to investigate cortical dynamics during a Go/NoGo task in PD patients with and without LID, compared with healthy volunteers. Thirty-six PD patients (18 LID-PD, 18 nLID-PD) and 20 healthy volunteers performed a Go/NoGo task during TMS-EEG, which assessed functional connectivity between the supplementary motor area (SMA) and primary motor cortex (M1), and cortical reactivity through TMS-evoked potentials. Healthy volunteers exhibited task-dependent modulation of SMA-M1 connectivity, with increased theta-band coupling during NoGo trials and gamma-band coupling during Go trials; this pattern was absent in both PD groups, particularly in those with dyskinesias. TMS-evoked potentials revealed enhanced N100 responses during NoGo trials in healthy volunteers, reduced in non-dyskinetic patients and absent in dyskinetic ones. SMA-M1 gamma connectivity correlated with motor performance and clinical severity. During post-TMS epochs, healthy volunteers showed context-dependent alpha/beta modulation that was disrupted in PD patients. SMA-M1 communication and cortical inhibitory processing are impaired in PD, especially in patients with dyskinesias. SMA dysfunction may represent a biomarker and therapeutic target for inhibitory deficits in PD.

title: Polystyrene nanoplastic exposure exacerbates epileptic vulnerability in SCN1A mutation models.
abstract: Micro- and nanoplastics are pervasive contaminants detected in human tissues that cross the blood-brain barrier to induce neuroinflammation, apoptosis, and neurotoxicity. Here, we examined whether polystyrene nanoplastic (PS-NP) exposure alters seizure susceptibility in SCN1A+/- cerebral organoids and Scn1a+/- mice, modeling the severe genetic epilepsy Dravet syndrome. At equal mass concentrations, 50 nm PS-NPs penetrated organoids more deeply and upregulated inflammatory and neurotoxic gene expression more robustly than 100 nm particles, inducing apoptotic activation and significant DNA fragmentation. Exposure disrupted steroid homeostasis-causing genotype-dependent cortisol elevations-and perturbed neurotransmitter systems in SCN1A-deficient models via reduced GABA and glutamate, accompanied by decreased GAD2 and increased VGLUT2 expression. In vivo, exposed Scn1a+/- mice exhibited hyperactivity and reached Racine stages 3-5 more rapidly under thermal induction, demonstrating a reduced seizure threshold. Pharmacological inhibition of 11β-hydroxysteroid dehydrogenase type 1 reversed this hyperactivity but failed to restore the seizure threshold. Together, these findings indicate that PS-NP exposure exacerbates seizure vulnerability in genetically susceptible backgrounds, accompanied by marked neurochemical, endocrine, and apoptotic disruptions. These results support a 'second-hit' model wherein environmental nanoplastics act as external triggers in genetic epilepsy, underscoring the vital need to incorporate gene-environment interactions into neurotoxicological risk assessments.

title: Mapping the structure and microstructure of the adolescent brain: Insights from the ABCD study.
abstract: The Adolescent Brain Cognitive Development (ABCD) Study provides an unprecedented opportunity to characterize adolescent brain maturation and its correlates. This review synthesizes structural and diffusion magnetic resonance imaging (MRI) findings from ABCD, emphasizing methodological advances and implications for mental health, obesity, and environmental risk. We first summarize ABCD's harmonized multi-site acquisition, high completion rates, and longitudinal coverage, highlighting the impact of quality control and scanner harmonization. Structural MRI work converges on largely linear cortical thinning from late childhood through early adolescence, surface area (SA) peaks in early adolescence followed by modest contraction, and regionally patterned but small associations with cognition, puberty, sex, and psychopathology. Genetic and twin analyses show that cortical thickness (CT) and SA are highly heritable yet partly dissociable, and that stable person-specific variance is not captured entirely by genetic influences. We then review diffusion imaging, focusing on Restriction Spectrum Imaging (RSI), which decomposes the diffusion signal into restricted, hindered, and free-water compartments and provides neurite- and cell-body-sensitive indices in both white and grey matter. ABCD RSI studies reveal widespread age-related increases in restricted diffusion in cortico-striatal-thalamic circuits and demonstrate that these microstructural signals are highly heritable in some brain regions. RSI also sharpens inferences about environmental and metabolic exposures: air pollution, central adiposity, and weight gain show associations with altered intracellular diffusion, particularly in reward circuitry. Finally, we describe FEMA, a fast mixed-effects framework that enables vertex- and voxelwise modeling at ABCD scale, and outline opportunities to integrate structural, diffusion, and genomic data into developmentally informed brain-behavior models.

title: The role of psychosocial stress on atypical visuoperceptual organization in individuals at clinical high risk for psychosis.
abstract: Alterations in visuoperceptual organization (VPO) occur across the psychosis spectrum, characterized by a loosening of visual context and breakdown in the integration of individual elements into percepts. Psychosocial stress is implicated in psychosis etiology and may also differentially affect perceptual processing, yet its relationship with VPO in individuals at clinical high-risk for psychosis (CHR-P) has not been examined. Participants (N=557; 343 CHR-P 214 healthy controls) were evaluated with clinical interviews, measures of cumulative life event stress and perceived stress over the past month, and computerized tasks assessing VPO at baseline. The Mooney Faces Task (MFT) is an ambiguous face detection task, and the Ebbinghaus Task assesses size illusion susceptibility. Multiple linear regressions examined associations among stress, VPO, and group. Both proximal (p = .034) and cumulative (p < .001) stress were associated with more faces reported, but not with facial demographic accuracy on inverted MFT trials. When modeled together, cumulative stress (p < .001) remained significantly associated with inverted faces, whereas proximal stress and group status were not. Cumulative stress was inversely related to context sensitivity in the Ebbinghaus Task (p = .002), and proximal stress was positively related to context sensitivity (p = .036). The proximal association attenuated after adjusting for age and sex (p = .052), and the cumulative association remained (p = .013). Findings suggest cumulative stress may be relevant to individual differences in VPO beyond psychosis risk status and impart differential effects on context sensitivity than proximal stress. Further investigation is needed to clarify proposed mechanisms and explore stress reduction and resilience-based interventions for CHR-P individuals.

title: Molecular mechanisms of lithium neuroprotection in Alzheimer's disease: A systematic comprehensive review.
journal: Journal of trace elements in medicine and biology : organ of the Society for Minerals and Trace Elements (GMS)
abstract: Alzheimer's disease (AD) contributes to most cases of dementia globally and is characterized by amyloid-β (Aβ) deposition, tau hyperphosphorylation, oxidative stress, and neuroinflammation. Existing treatments are merely management products that do not alter the course of the disease; thus, there is an urgent need to develop disease-modifying strategies for treating this condition. The multifaceted molecular effects of lithium have created new hope for neuroprotective interest in AD because of its wide utility in the treatment of mood disorders. Lithium also prevents the phosphorylation of glycogen synthase kinase-3β (GSK-3β), which in turn prevents tau pathology, mediates amyloid precursor protein (APP) processing, and regulates the interaction of β-catenin/Wnt to inhibit Aβ formation. Moreover, lithium helps maintain mitochondrial bioenergetics and calcium homeostasis, facilitates the autophagy of proteinaceous aggregates, and mediates microglial activity to reduce neuroinflammation. Preclinical and epidemiological evidence also indicates that lithium depletion may be an upstream regulator of AD pathophysiology, and that microdoses or modified formulations may help increase the safety and efficacy of lithium therapy. Although there is strong mechanistic and translational evidence, the clinical effects are inconsistent because of the narrow therapeutic window and lithium toxicity. Future directions include precision medicine, biomarker-guided treatment, and novel delivery systems that exploit the disease-mitigating effects of lithium in AD.

title: Mandatory national clinical audits as a tool to drive improvements in multiple sclerosis outcomes.
abstract: Multiple sclerosis (MS) is a complex, time-critical neuroinflammatory condition where diagnostic delays and suboptimal treatment lead to irreversible disability. Despite an international consensus on best practices, equitable access to specialist care remains highly variable. We explore how implementing mandatory, continuous national clinical audit can potentially eradicate unwarranted clinical variation, drive systemic policy reform, secure targeted investment in specialist MS services, and create a positive feedback loop over time as services evolve. Drawing upon the highly successful models in stroke and cancer, we demonstrate how continuous, prospective data collection functions as an agent of change. We apply these mechanisms to MS care, using the internationally endorsed MS Brain Health: Time Matters policy recommendations, consensus quality standards, and their associated Quality Improvement tool as a blueprint for a potential mandatory national audit. Other recent initiatives, such as the Norwegian MS Registry, German implementation surveys and the UK MS Trust's Generating Evidence in MS Services (GEMSS) programme, provide proof of concept that standardised measurement improves operational efficiency, reduces non-elective emergency admissions, and generates robust health economic data necessary for strategic MS-related healthcare commissioning. To ensure equitable, cost-effective care and unlock funding for multidisciplinary teams, healthcare systems should be encouraged to invest in the infrastructure required for mandatory, continuous national audits of MS and other brain health conditions.

title: Association of reproductive factors with disease severity in women with relapsing-remitting multiple sclerosis.
abstract: While reproductive factors have been linked to multiple sclerosis (MS) onset and activity, their association with disability remains unclear. We investigated the relationship between reproductive variables and MS severity, measured by the Age-Related Multiple Sclerosis Severity Score (ARMSS). in 242 Italian women with relapsing-remitting MS, reproductive factors (age at menarche, oral contraceptive use, full-term pregnancies and pregnancy losses) were collected through a structured environmental questionnaire. Associations with ARMSS were assessed using linear regression models. Key findings on obstetric factors were replicated in an independent cohort (n = 465). longer oral contraceptive use before MS onset was associated with lower ARMSS (β = -0.048; p-value = 3.6 × 10-3). Contrasting associations were observed for obstetric factors, with number of full-term pregnancies being associated with lower ARMSS (β = -0.35; p-value = 0.042), while pregnancy losses being associated with higher ARMSS (β = 0.61; p-value = 0.036). Consistently, women with full-term pregnancies only showed lower disability than those with pregnancy losses only (β = -0.72; p-value = 0.026). The association with full-term pregnancies was replicated in the validation cohort (β = -0.44; p-value = 6.55 × 10-3), as well as the lower ARMSS observed in women reporting full-term pregnancies only compared to those reporting pregnancy losses only (β = -0.49; p-value = 0.013). our results highlight how reproductive factors may contribute to individual variability in disease severity.

title: Specific language process or repurposed sensorimotor mechanism? Hypotheses on the evolution of language syntax.
abstract: The origin of language syntax remains one of the central open questions in neuroscience. Two competing views dominate the debate: that syntax emerged as a discrete, species-specific novelty (the saltationist view), or that it arose gradually through the repurposing of pre-existing sensorimotor circuits. Here we review evidence in favor of the gradualist hypothesis and propose that three convergent elements, rooted in the sensorimotor brain, provided the evolutionary substrate for language syntax. First, the progressive expansion of direct cortico-motoneuronal (CM) projections from primary motor cortex to spinal motoneurons freed motor control from the rigidity of prewired synergies, enabling flexible, hierarchically nested action sequences. Second, the premotor system - particularly monkey area F5, the homolog of human Broca's area - implements a goal-directed motor lexicon with mirror properties constituting a precondition for intentional communication. Third, during observation of others' actions, the mirror system must simultaneously maintain competing goal hypotheses and resolve them incrementally - a process we term "hyperprediction" - that is computationally analogous to syntactic parsing. We further argue that Broca's area is not a dedicated language hub but one node within a broader cortico-subcortical network: the basal ganglia implement hierarchical chunking and rule learning across motor and linguistic domains, as evidenced by shared neural substrates for tool use and language syntax. Finally, we propose that recursion is not language-specific, and that the co-evolution of hand morphology and cortico-basal ganglia circuits provides a mechanistically grounded account of how syntactic capacities emerged from sensorimotor precursors, with five falsifiable predictions testable by current methods.
